ProjectTitle: Alaska's March to Statehood: The Crafting of a Constitution
ProjectDesc: In 2009 Alaska celebrates 50 years of Statehood. Over the next five years the Alaska Humanities Forum will re-educate Alaskans about “The March to Statehood”: the story of how a vast, trackless territory with a tiny, determined diverse population joins America. We begin in 2004 with an exploration of the Alaska Constitution. Many scholars claim it is the nation’s culminating state governance document. This education effort will engage, perhaps in their final public service, the energies of a dwindling number of Alaska’s founders, the living "Heroes of History" still with us today.
ToSupport: A series of activities that explore the history of Alaska's 50 years of statehood including a teacher's institute, a history curriculum unit, a public lecture series, radio broadcasts and a grant program.
Participants: Ira Perman [Project Director]; Gregory Kimura [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: History of American Samoa: 1900 - 1977
ProjectDesc: The Amerika Samoa Humanities Council is very much interested in documenting the history of American Samoa from 1900 to 1977. It is our expectation to employ a group of three researchers and one historian from the state of Hawaii to assist in the project. The goal of the project is to advance the knowledge of the people of American Samoa of the principles that define our indigenous identity as American and Samoan through the study of history and culture in the 20th century.
ToSupport: Research on the history of American Samoa from 1900 - 1977, including the collection of historical documents, records, and artifacts; writing of a textbook including these materials for use by high school students; and an institute for teachers.
Participants: Minareta Thompson [Project Director]; Niualama Taifane [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: We the People: A Colorado Initiative
ProjectDesc: We the People: A Colorado Initiative consists of five programs: Request for Proposals for Program Grants, Chautauqua Speakers Bureau, High Plains Chautauqua, Young Chautauqua, and America Challenged: Bread Lines and Battle Lines Teacher Institute. CEH will use tested formats to develop and implement quality programs in relation to several new priorities: providing opportunities for children to research topics in American history; meeting the content needs of K-12 teachers; and increasing the emphasis across CEH programs in civics education and American history.
ToSupport: A teachers institute, "America Challenged: Bread Lines and Battle Lines," High Plains Chautauqua, Young Chautauqua, speakers bureau and a special grant opportunity for public programs.

ProjectTitle: The Importance and Power of Protest
ProjectDesc: The Delaware Humanites Forum will present programs, some by its own initiatives and others in partnership with similar agencies, to examine the concepts of disagreement and protest in all its socially acceptable forms: letters, songs, banners, marches, sit-ins, rallies, etc. The Bill of Rights, the U.S. Constitution, and theDeclaration of Independence, our letters of government, will be the foundation for each part of the variety of programs that will focus on the social action of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
ToSupport: Scholars in Residence Program for teams of scholars to work with middle and high school teachers and students using the Bill of Rights, the US Constitution and the Declaration of Independence to examine the concepts of disagreement and protest in American history.

ProjectTitle: Harlem Renaissance in Florida
ProjectDesc: The seminars, programs and publication in this proposal explore the historic significance and cultural contributions of the writers, artists and musicians of the Harlem Renaissance, in particular, Florida's Zora Neale Hurston, James Weldon Johnson and Augusta Savage. These programs and the publication will be designed to provide teachers and the general public with the opportunity to examine and analyze the movement's multidisciplinary work, its historical context and significance, and its impact on Florida culture, American culture and African-American culture.
ToSupport: Teacher institutes, Chautauqua public programming, and an issue of FORUM magazine on the topic of the Harlem Renaissance and its impact on Florida, American, and African-American culture.
Participants: Janine Farver [Project Director]; Ann Schoenacher [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: We the People: Teacher Workshops on American Literature, Biography, Art and Popular Culture
ProjectDesc: The Hawai’i Council will partner with at least four educational and cultural organizations to conduct teacher workshops aimed at elementary school teachers and teachers in language arts, literature and art classes. Each workshop will explore American Heritage through history, literature, biography, art or popular culture. Images, symbols and literary and artistic expressions of American identity, ideals and values will be integrated into lesson plans and classroom activities that engage students in understanding the conflicts and milestones behind the history of democracy in America.
ToSupport: Four workshops for elementary school teachers and teachers in language arts, literature and art to explore topics in American culture through history, literature, biography, art or popular culture.

ProjectTitle: Better Together: An Ethnic Heritage Initiative
ProjectDesc: Better Together: An Ethnic Heritage Initiative is a project designed to strengthen communities and connect Kansans by uncovering personal and community stories that tell a more complete and inclusive history of Kansas. Through an existing grants program intended to preserve local history, new grant funds will support projects that focus on collecting, preserving, and exhibiting the history of ethnic groups in Kansas. Museum professionals, historians, and folklorists will serve as consultants for oral history and research projects, collections initiatives, and the development of exhibits.
ToSupport: "Better Together: An Ethnic Heritage Initiative" to provide grants to nonprofits for basic research, oral history collection, museum collection and exhibition development, and public programs.

ProjectTitle: Prime Time Family Reading and Chautauqua Development
ProjectDesc: The Kentucky Humanities Council (KHC) requests $46,700 for Prime Time Family Reading Time and $14,250 for Kentucky Chautauqua. KHC is currently initiating Prime Time in partnership with the Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives in 8 county libraries. Our request would enable KHC to support Prime Time in 8 additional libraries during a second year and develop a track record on which to base future funding requests to private foundations. Our Chautauqua joins those of other councils nationally as a proven vehicle for teaching American history to all audiences.
ToSupport: Expansion of the "Prime Time" reading and discussion programs, providing programs in 16 libraries over two years, and the development and review of additional individual Chautauqua presentations.
Participants: Virginia Carter [Project Director]; Albert Chandler [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Massachusetts Moments: A Radio Almanac
ProjectDesc: The Massachusetts Foundation for the Humanities will produce "Mass Moments"—365 stories from Massachusetts history—for daily broadcast on radio stations across the state. The 60-sec spots will be written to attract a wide range of listeners. They will be read and mixed by experienced radio professionals. Some stories have national significance; others are important primarily in the history of the Bay State. The Internet will be used to provide greater depth. A website will be created with scripts, primary sources, images, maps, timelines, links, and an archive.
ToSupport: Research and writing of "Mass Moments," a collection of 365 stories from Massachusetts history for daily broadcast on radio stations across the state, with additional information provided on a "Mass Moments" website.

ProjectTitle: Exploring the Roots and Responsibilities of Democracy in the CNMI
ProjectDesc: The project is a targeted regrant program to increase knowledge among middle and junior high school students about the history surrounding the creation of the CNMI, its unique political status with the United States, and the responsibilities of individuals in a democratic society. Eligible schools, teachers, and organizations may apply for funding to support activities such as lectures by experts, site visits to democratic institutions, interviews with knowledgeable individuals, exploration of current issues through fora and discussion groups, and original research.
ToSupport: A grant program to increase knowledge among middle and junior high school students about the history of the Commonwealth, its relationship to the United States, and the responsibilities of individuals in a democratic society.
Participants: Elizabeth Rechebei [Project Director]; Herman Guerrero [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: From Sea to Shining Sea: American Expansion and Cultural Change, 1790-1850
ProjectDesc: "From Sea to Shining Sea: American Expansion and Cultural Change, 1790-1850" is the grand theme of Chautauqua in 2005 and 2006, coinciding with the Lewis and Clark bicentennial. Five scholars spend five days in a community, presenting first-person programs on William Clark, York, Sacagawea, John Jacob Astor, and Tecumseh, and offering twelve interpretive workshops for adults and children. Dolley Madison serves as each evening's moderator. The scholars emphasize the significant changes through which the nation went in those critical years.
ToSupport: The 2005-2006 North Dakota presentations of the Great Plains Chautauqua's program "From Sea to Shining Sea: American Expansion and Cultural Change, 1790-1850," coinciding with the Lewis and Clark bicentennial.
Participants: David Solheim [Project Director]; Lynn Davis [Project Director]; Janet Rowse [Project Director]; Jim Norris [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Oklahoma We the People
ProjectDesc: To advance the We the People initiative, the Oklahoma Humanities Council will develop special projects and expand the resources of existing programs for use well into the future. OHC will develop WTP projects through Requests for Proposals, the Great Plains Chautauqua, and the We the People Lectures. We will expand two successful programs by adding discussion themes to Let's Talk About It, Oklahoma and digitizing TRACKS exhibits for online use. Through these projects, OHC will advance the knowledge of the principles that define America.
ToSupport: Great Plains Chautauqua in 2005, We the People Lectures, and a grant initiative. The reading and discussion program will include topics on American democracy and traveling exhibits projects will be digitized.
Participants: Anita May [Project Director]; David Pettyjohn [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: 1. Encounters: The New Worlds of Lewis and Clark and 2. On Principle
ProjectDesc: $22,920 of our We the People Funds will be used to host a Teacher Institute examining Lewis and Clark’s Corps of Discovery expedition; a seminal event in the history and culture of America and particularly of the Pacific Northwest.Thirty teachers will attend the institute, and take new knowledge and resources back to their classrooms, improving education for more than 3,000 students. The remaining $34,900 will be used to launch a radio program that will help Oregonians talk about principles of democracy and examine the diversity of views and beliefs that we hold within those principles.
ToSupport: A teacher institute on the new worlds of Lewis and Clark, and a series of short radio spots, "On Principle," to illuminate what Oregonians think about defining American principles.

ProjectTitle: Our Stories, Our Future
ProjectDesc: “Our Stories, Our Future”will be a statewide initiative for stories from American history with urgent importance for our future. Centered in regrants, the initiative will be complemented by Commonwealth Speaker presentations on American history and two literature programs in the Read About It! book discussion series: “Facts in Fiction: The Civil War,” exploring the war through the genre of historical fiction; and “American Life Stories,” exploring the diverse peoples who make up America. through the genre of memoir.
ToSupport: Speaker presentations and book discussions on topics in American history and a grant program to support projects that explore the contemporary relevance of the nation's founding documents.
Participants: Joseph Kelly [Project Director]; Laurie Zierer [Project Director]; Laurie Zierer [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Reappraise a collection of books related to the incorporation of Puerto Rico as a territory
ProjectDesc: ﻿Stimulate a reappraisal of a critical period in American history publishing facsimile editions of books and reports about the Island of Puerto Rico made available between 1899 and 1903 after the Spanish- American War. A series of workshops and conferences will be planned to acquaint History and Social Studies school teachers and History and Social Sciences university professors with the content, historical period and relevance of these sources.
ToSupport: Preservation, publication and distribution of books and reports originally published between 1899 and 1903 that explore the history of Puerto Rico after the Spanish-American War.
Participants: Miguel Rodriguez [Project Director]; Luis Gonzalez-Vales [Project Director]

Institution: Rhode Island Council for the Humanities
ProjectTitle: The Pursuit of Happiness: An Inquiry into Our Nation's Founding Principles
ProjectDesc: Codifying the values that would guide our nation in the “Declaration of Independence, ” Thomas Jefferson named “life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness” among the fundamental rights guaranteed to Americans. Taking inspiration from these words, RICH will engage Rhode Islanders across the state in an investigation into our nation’s founding principles of “life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness” beginning in September 2004. RICH seeks $44,330 in “We the People” funds to support: a regrants initiative, a public forums radio series, a film series, and a public television series.
ToSupport: A series of activities that explore the principles of "life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness" including a grant program, a radio and public television series, and a student poster/essay contest.

ProjectTitle: We the People of Tennessee: Telling Our Stories Digitally
ProjectDesc: “We the People of Tennessee: Telling our Stories Digitally” will create a model for making the results of local history projects accessible through the World Wide Web. The project will involve an urban neighborhood and three-county rural area, but the technology of the two projects and the final product will be the same: an internet-accessible database containing files for data and narratives about places, people, organizations, art and artifacts, and historical events and groups of events, all related to each other, and tied to a map through Geographical Information Systems.
ToSupport: To develop a model for a relational database available on the Internet for community history projects being done in the three-county rural Tennessee Overhill and Nashville's more urban Rutledge Hill neighborhood.
Participants: Terry Davis [Project Director]; Jane Walters [Project Director]; Kathryn Stephenson [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: U.S. Virgin Islanders: A People's Quest for Self-Governance
ProjectDesc: The people of the United States Virgin Islands have been struggling with self-determination since 1917. Although legislation since then has extended the political rights of our citizens, we are still, technically, a colony without a constitution. To deepen public awareness and understanding about the issues shaping our political future, the Virgin Islands Humanities Council is requesting $27,874 in order to plan and sponsor a lecture/discussion series, a video series, and an essay contest.
ToSupport: A series of activities, including a scholarly conference, public lecture series, oral history interviews, and a student essay contest, that explore questions of self-determination, political process and national identity.

ProjectTitle: Sharing Our Past, Shaping Our Future
ProjectDesc: Between September 1 2004 and December 31 2005, the Vermont Humanities Council (VHC) proposes to use We The People (WTP) funds to strengthen and augment the programmatic offerings of our three flagship program formats: reading and discussion programs, public lectures and presentations, and grants. Consistent with WTP guidelines, the programs will “explore significant events and themes in American history and culture, and… advance knowledge of the principles that define America.”
ToSupport: A special grant program, reading and discussion programs, and public lectures that explore significant themes and events in American history and culture.

ProjectTitle: We The People
ProjectDesc: Humanities Washington seeks funding of $61,750 in outright funds and $10,000 in matching funds to support WE THE PEOPLE “WTP” projects. We plan to use the funding in a variety of ways in order to provide WTP programs to the broadest spectrum of Washingtonians. We will use the funds to award re-grants for projects that respond to a Request for Proposals for the WTP initiative and support WTP presentations through our speakers’ bureau. Matching funds will support an initiative recognizing the 50th anniversary of the landmark Supreme Court decision, Brown vs. Board of Education.
ToSupport: The "Inquiring Minds" speakers bureau program on themes related to We the People; a special program of grants related to the initiative's goals; and special programming focused on the landmark Supreme Court Brown vs. Board of Education decision.

ProjectTitle: We the People
ProjectDesc: The WCH proposes:1)a teacher institute on the topic of comparative democracy,"Democracy in Greece and After:From Athens to America," 2)a partnership project with Wyoming Public Radio regarding a state- wide discussion on the face of change in Wyoming,"A Wyoming Conversation,"and 3)a re-grants program inviting grant applications on cultural diversity and projects to preserve/provide access to documents/ artifacts of local history in Wyoming.Projects are based on 2004 "Community Conversations"conducted by the WCH to solicit council priorities relating to community/statewide needs.
ToSupport: A teacher institute on the history of democracy from ancient Greece to modern America and "A Wyoming Conversation" that includes statewide discussions and a radio program co-sponsored by Wyoming Public Radio.
Participants: Marcia Britton [Project Director]; Victoria Sherry [Project Director]; Shannon Smith [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Material Culture Collection
ToSupport: Purchasing storage shelves and supplies to house 193 pairs of cross county and alpine skiing and snowboarding boots dating from the early 1900s to the present that relate to the history and culture of skiing in Vermont.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Needs Assessment of Photo Archive
ToSupport: A preservation needs assessment of the Calvin Littlejohn Photographic Archive at the Center for American History (CAH), which documents the history and culture of Fort Worth's African-American community, ca.1930 through 1980.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Collections of Maryland History
ToSupport: The purchase of acid-free storage materials for eleven collections of papers related to the history of Maryland and the mid-Atlantic, ranging from the 18th to the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Survey
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of archives that document the local history of Gloucester, Massachusetts, from 1634 to 1874.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring of Material Culture Collections
ToSupport: Purchasing environmental monitoring equipment to preserve material culture collections related to the history and culture of central Indiana.
Participants: Kari Price [Project Director]; Jill Lesh [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring Program Initiative
ToSupport: An environmental survey of the Carnegie-Vincent Library and the Abraham Lincoln Library and Museum, which document Abraham Lincoln's life and times, local and regional history, and the history of the university.
Participants: Donna Bible [Project Director]; Cheryl Scott [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Environmental and Storage Improvements
ToSupport: Hiring a conservation consultant to train staff and purchasing environmental monitoring equipment, storage furniture and materials to rehouse textiles, paper collections, and objects of material culture that relate to the history of ranching in Colorado.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the papers of Jesus T. Piñero, who became the first native-born governor of Puerto Rico in 1946.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Special Collections and Archives
ToSupport: A comprehensive preservation survey of the university archives and an assessment of its special collection related to aviation history, and the history of the city of Dayton and of the Miami Valley of Ohio.

ProjectTitle: Assessment of Wooden Furnishings
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of upholstered furniture and wooden furnishings in the Nichols House, an 1804 house museum in Boston.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring Project
ToSupport: The purchase and installation of environmental monitoring equipment to provide information about the fluctuation of temperature and humidity in a facility containing archives relating to a fuel and iron company, 1872-1990s.

Institution: Lillian and Albert Small Capital Jewish Museum, Inc.
ProjectTitle: Rehousing Archival Collections
ToSupport: The purchase of storage shelving and preservation supplies to rehouse a collection of correspondence, sermons, publications, photographs, and memorabilia related to 20th-century Jewish history in Montgomery County, Maryland.

ProjectTitle: Survey of University Archives
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the Dupont Library's audio and video materials, maps, blueprints, museum items, and art, related to the university, the affiliated Episcopal Church, Sewanee, and the many writers associated with it.

ProjectTitle: Rehouse Printed Works in American History Collection
ToSupport: The purchase of supplies to rehouse 2,750 printed works that document American life from the 17th century to the present.

Institution: Research Foundation for the State University of New York
ProjectTitle: Collections Storage Upgrade and Environmental Monitoring
ToSupport: The purchase of light and environmental monitoring equipment as well as supplies to re-house American and European works of art on paper.

ProjectTitle: Museum Library Preservation Assessment
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the museum's library and archival collections, which focus on the history of railroads in the Pacific Northwest.

Institution: Museum of Chinese in the Americas
ProjectTitle: Preservation of Historic Chinese Costumes
ToSupport: Consultation with a conservator who will develop a preservation plan for 77 Chinese dresses custom-tailored in the 1930s and 1940s and 26 intricate Chinese opera costumes from New York City's oldest Chinese opera club.

ProjectTitle: Storage Planning Project
ToSupport: Planning for the improved storage of humanities collections, which include 28,000 artifacts that represent the history and culture of the San Juan Basin in Colorado.

ProjectTitle: Emergency Preparedness Training and Rehousing Historic Documents
ToSupport: Purchasing storage materials, an environmental data logger, and light filters, and hiring a consultant to conduct a workshop on emergency preparedness, response and recovery to preserve a collection of documents on the history of the university, the town of Lawton, and Native Americans.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment of Film Archives
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of archival moving image and paper-based materials, dating to the latter half of the 20th century, which would provide a basis for developing long-term conservation, preservation, and cataloging plans.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Manuscript Collection
ToSupport: The purchase of hanging files and storage cabinets for the manuscript collections of the Traditional Arts Research Collection in the Michigan State University Museum.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Latin Music Collection
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of rare periodicals, music manuscripts, graphic prints, and ephemera that reflect the history and theory of Afro-Caribbean Latin music.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing the Historic Silver Collection
ToSupport: The purchase of two storage cabinets to house the Folgers Coffee Silver Collection, a group of 96 English silver coffee pots and serving accessories dating from the 18th and early 19th centuries.

ProjectTitle: Conservation Assessment of Historical Collections
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of 200 rare circus posters that date from 1882 to the 1980s.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Collections
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of collections at the college archives that are related to Baptist, Presbyterian, Methodist, and Lutheran history in the American Northwest. The college archivist would also attend a preservation workshop.

Institution: Association for the Preservation of Virginia Antiquities
ProjectTitle: Collections Care Planning
ToSupport: Consultation with a conservator to develop a storage plan for material culture collections that document the history of Virginia from 1607 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Assessment of African-American Art Collections
ToSupport: A workshop on the basic preservation of art collections, a preservation assessment of paintings and works on paper, and the purchase of a light meter and light-filtering muslin to preserve a collection by modern African American artists.

Institution: House of Seven Gables Settlement Association
ProjectTitle: Preservation of the Nathaniel Hawthorne Collection
ToSupport: Consultation with a conservator and the purchase of storage supplies and shelving for the Nathaniel Hawthorne collection, which includes documents, personal belongings, and books pertaining to Hawthorne.

ProjectTitle: Records Management Project
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and one-day workshop to preserve archives that document the local history of Lavaca County, Texas, from 1846 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Archival Preservation Project
ToSupport: The purchase of storage equipment and preservation supplies to rehouse archival records, photographs, maps, and other materials related to family, mining, labor, and legal history of the area surrounding Red Lodge, Montana, from the1880s to the 1970s.

ProjectTitle: Humanities Collections Preservation Planning Survey
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of 526 linear feet of institutional archives and 209 linear feet of special collections related to Catholic education and to the university's history.

ProjectTitle: Architectural and design Collections Rehousing
ToSupport: No to support statement

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of archival and artifact collections related to a school for African Americans in Virginia from 1866 to 1966. There would also be a workshop on basic preservation and archival practices.

Institution: Hubbard Museum of the American West
ProjectTitle: Rehousing of Artifacts in Collections Storage
ToSupport: Purchasing storage furniture and materials to rehouse material culture collections that relate to the history and culture of southern New Mexico.

ProjectTitle: Conservation Assessment of Historic Works on Paper
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of 40 European works of art on paper ranging in date from the 15th to the 19th centuries.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of the Ancient Egyptian Collection
ToSupport: An assessment of the Robert F. Fullerton Art Museum's preservation efforts, the treatment needs of Egyptian ceramic artifacts, and training of staff and volunteers.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Photographic Collections
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of nine photographic collections comprising images documenting architecture, graphic design, national and international expositions, and travel that illustrate the social history and culture of North America and Europe.

ProjectTitle: On-Site Consultation and Training
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment and on-site training workshop on the care of material culture collections that relate to the history and culture of south-central Wyoming.
Participants: Palma Jack [Project Director]; Denise Patton [Project Director]

Institution: Hot Springs County Museum and Cultural Center
ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment and Training Workshop
ToSupport: Hiring a consultant to conduct an assessment of storage conditions and a training workshop. The project would also purchase storage furniture and preservation materials for collections that relate to the history and culture of central Wyoming.

ProjectTitle: Audio Archive Assessment Project
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the organization's audio collection that focuses on the history and culture of the Puget Sound region of the American Northwest, and includes public forums, economic and political programs, music, documentaries, and interviews since 1962.

Institution: National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum, Inc.
ProjectTitle: Preservation Storage
ToSupport: The purchase of storage materials to rehouse objects related to American popular culture.

Institution: City and County of Butte-Silver Bow
ProjectTitle: Disaster Response Planning
ToSupport: Hiring a consultant to produce a disaster preparedness/emergency response plan and the purchase of supplies to ensure the long-term care of 12,500 linear feet of archives related to mining, labor, and local history, 1860 to 1990.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of original television programs and selected unedited footage created since 1968 by the university's public broadcasting station. The videotapes document local, regional, and national events, history, and culture.

ProjectTitle: Preserving Oral History Holdings
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of audio recordings created from the 1950s through 1970s that document political, historical, and cultural events in Puerto Rico.

ProjectTitle: Assessment of the Library Development Records
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and three one-day workshops for archives that document the formation and growth of library service in Mississippi from 1926 to the present.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment and Planning
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of books, pamphlets, catalogs, objects, and ephemera related to the history of the university and business education in Ohio in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

Institution: Albany Institute of History and Art
ProjectTitle: Library Preservation Survey
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of the library collections and the physical facility housing documents and objects related to the history of Albany and the Hudson Valley since the 18th century.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Needs Assessment Project
ProjectDesc: We seek funding for a consulting archivist to perform a collection survey of Goddard College Archives. The consultant will assess the preservation needs and environmental and storage conditions. The project will also include a review of existing policies and practices pertaining to access and use, and security. The goal is to develop a long-range plan that will allow us to address the overall preservation, access and security needs of the collection. Due to its uniqueness, the archives is the library’s preeminent collection. It documents the rich history of Goddard College. Most documents are in loose-leaf paper format and were gathered from former office files. Also included are a collection of photographs and a mixed A/V collection.
ToSupport: An assessment of the preservation, disaster response, security, and facility needs of the library as well as a review of collection policies and practices for archives related to the history of the college.

Institution: Sisters of Charity of St. Augustine Archives
ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment for Archives
ProjectDesc: A general preservation planning assessment of the archival holdings of the Sisters of Charity of St. Augustine(CSA)with attention to: the 19th and early 20th century documents (1851-1926) pertaining to the early life and works of CSA;the Heritage room which contains artifacts from this period;collections from the mid-20th century documenting two sisters who were significant figures in Northeast OH. The written report of the external, qualified consultant would identify and prioritize recommended actions which would be part of a long-range plan for improving the environmental conditions of the documents and the continued preservation of the holdings, thus improving accessibility for internal and external publics, particularly historians.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment to ensure the long-term care of archives and objects related to the history of a Roman Catholic women's religious order, 1851 to 1926.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Negatives in Photograph Collection
ProjectDesc: We wish to purchase photographic negative sleeves to rehouse negatives in our Lane Photograph Collection. We completed a general conservation survey in December 2003, funded by a CAP Grant from the IMLS. The first recommendation in the executive summary of the report is to use archival-quality long-term storage supplies. Conservator Brian Ramer specifically identified a need to rehouse our photographic negatives in appropriate archival supplies. They are currently in archival storage boxes but not in archivally approved sleeves. Our collections manager will direct this project using our staff, volunteers and interns.
ToSupport: The purchase of supplies to rehouse negatives in the Walter B. Lane Photograph Collection focusing on regional Pennsylvania history in the latter half of the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Assessment of Photograph Collection
ProjectDesc: Assessing Hildene's Lincoln Family Photograph Collection will give us the information we need to properly conserve and store our 1,500 photographs of the Abraham and Mary Todd Lincoln family and descendants dating approximately from the mid-1840s to the late-1970s. These photographs chronicle over 130 years of very important American and Lincoln Family history. Using the information that results from this assessment, we will create a plan of work and execute the preservation and storage activities suggested.
ToSupport: Consultation with a conservator to work with the repository's staff to safeguard and rehouse images dating from the 1840s through the 1970s in the organization's Lincoln Family Photograph Collection.
Participants: Beth Meachem [Project Director]; Brian Knight [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Preservation of Special Collections
ProjectDesc: The proposed project of the Newport News Public Library System is composed of a preservation assessment and a collections care training session conducted by a professional conservator. The portion of the Martha Woodroof Hiden Memorial Virginiana Collection which is considered rare and irreplaceable will be assessed. The items to be reviewed are the Old Dominion Land Company Records, the World War I related documents, map and the scrap book collections. These materials are dated from 1828-1988. The conservator will provide a written report with priorities. The conservator will also conduct an one day session on collection care for the three staff members who work within the Martha Woodroof Hiden Memorial Collection.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of archives, manuscripts, maps, and other records related to the history of Newport News, Virginia, from the 1820s to the 1980s. A workshop would educate staff on proper preservation procedures.

ProjectTitle: Preservation of Archives
ProjectDesc: In an effort to preserve the historical past of the Geneva, Indiana area for future generations, the Geneva Public Library proposes to employ Noraleen A. Young, a public historian and certified archivist with expertise in the areas of archival administration, preservation, and related fields, to advise the library director in assessing the local history collection. This assessment would include a long-term plan for the care of the collection, a determination of the best and most cost effective preservation methods, an initial purchase of the most essential supplies, training of the director and other members of the staff and volunteers through a combination of in-house training and participation in regional preservation workshops.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and creation of a management plan for the care of archives related to Indiana history. A consultant would also conduct training in the management and preservation of archives for library staff.

ProjectTitle: Conservation Training Workshop and Environmental Analysis
ProjectDesc: The New England Quilt Museum is requesting support for preservation activites recommended by a 2003 General Conservation Assessment (CAP). The first component of the project is to have a professional conservator train our staff and volunteers in the basic tasks related to the storage of quilts and their preparation for display. The conservator will also prepare a binder of reference materials that will serve the as a collections manual for the museum. The second component of the project is to have a consultant evaluate the data collected from a year of environmental monitoring. The consultant will make recommendations and help us create a long-range plan for environmental control at the museum.
ToSupport: Consultation with conservators who will provide preservation training for staff and volunteers on environmental monitoring and on the storage and display of quilts.

Institution: Eiteljorg Museum of American Indians and Western Art, Inc.
ProjectTitle: Rehousing Historic Native American Clothing and Textiles
ProjectDesc: The Eiteljorg Museum has a distinctive collection of Native American objects related to native cultures of North America. Within this collection is a select group of clothing and textile items which are temporarily stored on open shelves made of foam core. Access to Native American culture bearers and other researchers is limited, handling is difficult and potentially harmful and the objects are exposed to light, dust and other elements. This project, following recommendations from a CAP grant, will re-house a significant part of the collection in a cabinet--designed to maximum conservation standards--which will resolve these problems and better preserve these objects.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture and rehousing of 75 American Indian clothing and textile items, which date from the 1840s to the 1920s.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Needs Assessment of Historical Collections
ProjectDesc: The Town of Winchester, under the direction of the Town Clerk and with the collaboration of the Winchester Historical Society and the Winchester Public Library, proposes to hire a consultant to conduct a preservation needs assessment of its historical collections. The consultant will survey three sites: Town Hall (Archival Center, two storage vaults, Engineering and Planning Departments, and offices of the Town Clerk); Public Library (Local History Room); and the Sanborn House (artifacts formerly part of the archives). The final report will address general condition of the collections, environment, housing, security, emergency preparedness, access, and use with recommendations for a collaborative long-term preservation and management plan.
ToSupport: A preservation and access assessment at three sites for archival, artifact, and special library collections that reflect the history of Winchester, Massachusetts, from the 18th to 20th centuries.

ProjectTitle: Collections Storage Furniture
ProjectDesc: This proposal requests support for replacement of a wooden storage unit with a nickel-plated wire rack system and corresponding sizes of textile and archival print boxes. Bennington Museum is currently equipped with a considerable amount of inappropriate storage furniture including a 38-foot span of painted wooden drawers, which hold fragile textiles, paper ephemera, toys, fans, and other objects. All of these objects are susceptible to acids. While the objects are tissue-wrapped and drawers lined with muslin, discoloration to the linens demonstrates the presence of acid migration. Currently, objects are also very difficult to access, to get to one object, many other objects must be moved, which causes unnecessary wear.
ToSupport: Purchasing storage furniture and materials to preserve material culture collections that relate to the history and culture of southern Vermont and New England.

ProjectTitle: Conservation Assessment of Rare Book Collection
ProjectDesc: Two expert consultants will make a conservation assessment of SPNEA’s Rare Book Collection. The work will focus on the collection’s environmental needs, proper cleaning & handling, space & housing requirements, and identify any titles needing immediate treatment. Included will be a long-term conservation plan for 2,000 16th to 20th century titles in the Collection, and individualized treatment proposals for approximately 50 titles selected by SPNEA’s Curator of Library & Archives. Project opportunities for future interns will also be identified. Estimated time required is 4 days on-site and 3.5 days off-site work. This conservation assessment project will ensure both the preservation and accessibility of this important collection.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of the rare book collection of architectural history, which will identify immediate conservation treatment needs and develop a long-term conservation plan.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Survey of Archival Collections
ProjectDesc: The Lincoln Public Library will hire a preservation consultant to perform a general preservation survey of the paper-based local history materials stored in the library's historical archive. The archive contains both published and unpublished materials relating to all aspects of the history of Lincoln and serves as the town's archive. Lincoln was settled long before the American Revolution and was originally part of Concord. The preservation consultant's report will assess possible risks to the collection, evaluate institutional policies and procedures, and identify preservation priorities. This report will be used as a planning document for the Lincoln Public Library's preservation activities to save these materials for future generations.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of books, archives, photographs, maps, newspapers, and audio and videotapes related to the history of Lincoln, Massachusetts, from 1754 to the late 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Map Collection
ProjectDesc: The Map Collection of the Long Island Division, Queens Borough Public Library, New York, consists of approximately 3,500 maps, documenting the geography of Kings (Brooklyn), Queens, Nassau and Suffolk Counties from 1637-2004. The maps detail the island’s vast physical and social changes over the past two centuries. Their current condition and storage arrangement make them difficult for researchers to access. The division is seeking a Preservation Assistance Grant to hire a consultant to perform a survey of the Map Collection. The consultant will produce a report addressing the Collection’s preservation and conservation needs, including its storage, handling, treatment, reformatting, future exhibition and more.
ToSupport: A preservation survey of a map collection that documents the Long Island area of New York from 1634 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Art and Archives Collections
ProjectDesc: The Fairbanks Museum will produce a preservation plan for works on paper representing the watercolors and archives of internationally known 20th century German painter, Helmut Siber, who lived in northern New England during the 1960’s and early 1970’s and produced a large body of work interpreting the region’s dramatic weather. The Museum seeks to engage a paper conservator to produce a condition assessment of these materials and recommendations for their future housing, conservation, and exhibition. The Museum seeks to enhance public opportunities for study and interpretation of Siber’s work as it pertains to the observation and appreciation of natural phenomena and his evolving ideas on aesthetics, science, and artistic technique.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and the purchase of boxes and other supplies to re-house the museum's manuscript papers and watercolor collection of 20th-century German artist, Helmut Siber.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Improvements and Staff Training at Three Repositories
ProjectDesc: The Littleton Historical Society, the Reuben Hoar Library and the Town of Littleton having jointly completed work on a historical records survey, “Preserving Littleton’s Legacy”, under a grant from the Massachusetts Historical Records Advisory Board., now wish to put the recommendations of the survey into practice to “Protect Littleton’s Legacy”. Valuable materials would be cleaned and protected from dirt and wear by phase boxes, archival folders and containers. Access and use policies would be established. Staff members would be trained in collection maintenance including monitoring the heat and humidity in the storage areas and taking action on the results.
ToSupport: Consultation to develop policies and procedures for the care and use of records that document the municipal history of Littleton, Massachusetts, from 1715 to the present. The grant would also support the purchase of environmental monitoring equipment, a HEPA vacuum, ultra violet light filters and other supplies, and provide staff training.

ProjectTitle: Records Center Preservation Assessment
ProjectDesc: The City of Las Cruces Records Center will hire a consultant to evaluate and make recommendations on environmental and procedural methods. This will enable the development of short and long-term preservation strategies for historical city records. As the only municipal records center in southern New Mexico, the Records Center’s project ensures the preservation of documents that are a rich source of the history of southern New Mexico.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment for archives that document the history of Las Cruces, New Mexico, from the early 1900s to the present.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Archival Collections
ProjectDesc: The library’s Local History Room houses a unique collection of rare books, photographs, local maps and postcards. The items preserve some of the history of Somerset and Morris counties as well that of the Borough of Bernardsville, a town steeped in rich history. A conservator’s evaluation of the materials housed in the Local History Room via the state Historical Commission’s Caucus Archival Projects Evaluation (CAPES) stated specific preservation needs to prevent further deterioration of the items. Funding is not available in the library’s budget to meet these needs. This funding request is for the basic supplies recommended in that CAPES evaluation as necessary to maintain and preserve this collection.
ToSupport: The purchase of preservation supplies to rehouse books, scrapbooks, photographs, and maps related to local history.

ProjectTitle: Preserving the Louisiana Supreme Court Archives
ProjectDesc: The proposed project will clean and rehouse in acid-free file folders and boxes 4,881 case files created by the Louisiana Supreme Court from 1890 through 1904. The case files currently are stored in the acidic envelopes and boxes in which they were received from the Court in 2000, and they contain metal fasteners and staples.
ToSupport: The purchase of boxes and file folders to re-house the Supreme Court of Louisiana archives dating from 1890 to 1904.

Institution: State of New Hampshire Department of Resources and Economic Development
ProjectTitle: Preserving Material Culture Collections
ProjectDesc: The Wentworth-Coolidge Commission, by authorization of the State Division of Parks and Recreation, had undertaken testing variants of ultra-violet (UV) filters and room-darkening shades for the protection of the interiors and artifacts in the Wentworth-Coolidge Mansion, a National Historic Landmark. The UV protection test project was funded by an NEH Preservation Assistance grant. The State seeks a grant to purchase permanent and durable preservation supplies for UV protection. The light control system is based upon the results of the test project and the recommendations of the preservation consultant, the site Executive Director, and the State Historical Resources office.
ToSupport: The installation of light filtering film and interior shades on windows in the 18th-century Wentworth Coolidge Mansion to protect collections from exposure to light.

ProjectTitle: Collection Rehousing
ProjectDesc: The successful completion of this project will result in the total replacement of all storage media used in housing the collections of the 99s Museum of Women Pilots which document the role and achievements of women pilots throughout aviation history. Grant proceeds will be used for immediate purchase of storage boxes, shelving, and preservation supplies, supplanting continuing remodeling and upgrading of the collections storage area.
ToSupport: Purchasing preservation materials to rehouse material culture collections related to the history of women in aviation.
Participants: Nancy Clark [Project Director]; Carolyn Smith [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment of Archives
ProjectDesc: The Lee Strasberg Creative Center wishes to utilize consultants to provide a general preservation assessment of the institution’s collections, which include original correspondence, manuscripts, photographs, and audio/visual materials. One consultant will focus on the paper-based materials, while the other will survey the media materials. ToSupport: The arrangement, description, and minor repairs to 26,400 black-and-white photographic negatives that document African-American history and culture in Pittsburgh from 1935 through 1975. A searchable Internet-accessible catalog and finding aids would be created and 28,000 digitized positive images would also be mounted on the Internet.

ProjectTitle: A Database of Mutsun, an Extinct California American Indian Language
ProjectDesc: This project will encode all archival information about the extinct Mutsun language into two databases. Mutsun is a Costanoan Native American language, spoken in the San Francisco area until 1930. Several early linguists recorded vast quantities of information about Mutsun, but this information, although on microfilm, is inaccessible because it is in the form of unanalyzed fieldnotes, primarily handwritten. The project will enter all of the archival information into an annotated text database and a dictionary database, producing a hard copy dictionary and hard copy annotated text publication as well as searchable databases. These products will be of great benefit to the Mutsun people, to other Native American groups, and to linguists.
ToSupport: The transcription and encoding of field notes on the extinct language of the Mutsun, a California Indian tribe, resulting in a text database and a lexical/dictionary database, to be available also in print.

ProjectTitle: Compilation of the Repertoire International de la Presse Musicale, 1900-1950 [RIPM]
ProjectDesc: While an “urgent need” for the retrospective indexing of music periodicals has been recognized since the 1930s it was not before the early 1980s that RIPM was established to undertake this task. Initially focusing on 19th-century music journals, RIPM has, since 1988, produced 173 volumes and an online database of some 450,000 annotated records. In 2003, RIPM expanded its scope to 1950 and took the first significant step toward filling the widely-acknowledged “access gap” in music periodical literature published between 1900 and the beginning of the modern indexing projects (1949). This grant would permit RIPM to continue its work on 20th-century music periodicals, and to produce twelve volumes and the equivalent data in electronic formats.
ToSupport: The compilation of twelve volumes documenting music and musical life in Europe and the United States during the first half of the twentieth century.

ProjectTitle: Preserving the Salisbury Collection in Near Eastern Studies
ProjectDesc: The Salisbury Collection began in 1870 with a gift from Edward Elbridge Salisbury, the first professor of Arabic Languages and Culture at Yale College. It has grown over the years into a comprehensive collection of foundational works on Islamic law, history, religion, science, mathematics and poetry, along with a large collection of European imprints that document European scholars' first systematic study of Arab religions, language and cultures. The project will enable us to repair those items that are repairable, mass deacidify those volumes that are on acidic paper but have not yet become brittle, and to microfilm those volumes that can no longer be handled without losing information due to brittleness or fragility.
ToSupport: The preservation microfilming and cataloging of 2,500 of the 16,000 embrittled volumes in the Edward E. Salisbury Collection of Arabic languages and culture, and minor conservation treatment of an additional 1,400 volumes.

Institution: Trustees of Columbia University in the City of New York
ProjectTitle: Preserving and Making Accesible the Barbara C. Adachi Collection of Bunraku, Japanese Theater
ProjectDesc: Columbia University Libraries proposes a 2-year project to organize, preserve, and make accessible the Barbara C. Adachi Bunraku (Japanese Puppet Theater) Collection. This collection is one the most extensive in the world documenting the rich performance tradition of bunraku, which has been recognized by UNESCO as a "masterpiece" of humanity. Bunraku dates back to the 17th century; this collection documents its revival in the second half of the 20th century, through more than 12,500 slides and nearly 7,000 black-and-white photographs of rehearsals and performances, as well as textual and audio materials. The collection's significance for research and teaching spans a number of fields: literature, drama, history, cultural studies, and more.
ToSupport: The arrangement, description, rehousing, and cataloging of a multimedia collection that documents the history of Japanese puppet theater from 1960 through the 1990s. An Internet-accessible finding aid would be created in English and Japanese.

Institution: Trustees of Columbia University in the City of New York
ProjectTitle: Preservation Microfilming of Slavic Culture and History
ProjectDesc: Columbia University Libraries proposes the two-year Slavic Culture and History Project, Phase IV, to preserve brittle, damaged Slavic-language materials. These materials are in the subject areas of Russian and East European history and literature published between 1850 and 1960. Columbia's holdings in this area are among the top five in the nation, and are in constant demand by researchers locally, nationally, and internationally. The project goal is to create archival-quality master microfilms with a potential lifespan of hundreds of years and to store them in conditions optimized for longevity. A total of 2,300 monograph volumes and 3,450 serial volumes comprising approximately 2,248 titles will be microfilmed.
ToSupport: The preservation microfilming and cataloging of 5,200 brittle Slavic-language volumes published from 1850 to 1960 and held in the university's Russian and East European collections.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Microfilming of The New York Public Library's Collection on the United States Banking and Finance Industry

The proposed project will preserve 8,000 monographs, published between the late-18th century and the mid-20th century, that are endangered by rapid deterioration. The project will produce approximately 1.2 million frames of microfilm over two years, preserving 2.4 million pages of text. The project will build upon eight other Brittle Books projects at The New York Public Library, funded by the NEH, beginning in 1989 and continuing to the present.
ToSupport: The preservation microfilming of 4,000 deteriorating volumes on the history of banking and finance in the United States published from 1800 to 1950.

ProjectTitle: Preserve and Create Online Access to Historic Acetate and Nitrate Negatives within the GE Photograph Collection
ProjectDesc: The Schenectady Museum & Planetarium will create an educational web site, "Inventing Modern America," utilizing images from the Museum's GE Photograph Collection and additional materials from the Museum's International Technology Archives. The Museum will preserve, re-house and refrigerate or freeze more than 81,000 acetate and nitrate negatives that have been identified by a photograph conservator as being at-risk. The Museum will create access to the negatives by digitizing and cataloging a selection of 12,000 negatives and creating a searchable online database for its collections.
ToSupport: Digitizing and cataloging 12,000 General Electric Company photographs dated 1892-1971, and developing a Web site featuring the images, which depict the impact of electric power on 20th-century American life. Additionally, purchase of cold storage units, boxes, and folders to rehouse 68,000 acetate and 12,000 nitrate negatives.

ProjectTitle: Japan Confronts the Aging Society
Program: Fellowships for Advanced Social Science Research on Japan
ProjectDesc: I propose to study old-age policy making, and policy, in Japan. The project will include an account of major policy changes from 1990 until now, concentrating on the initiation and implementation of the public, mandatory long-term-care insurance (LTCI) system that started in 2000; and an analysis of at least two reform processes that will be underway while I am in Japan. These are comprehensive pension reform, perhaps even including integration (already getting underway), and the scheduled 5th-year LTCI review (to be drafted in 2005 for implementation in 2006). The product will be a book that explains what the Japanese government has done about the aging-society problem, and how and why it did it. The first part of the book, perhaps 80-100 pages, will be an account of old-age policy from the mid-1950s until 1990, as summarized from my book of several years ago. This will be followed by four or five chapters based on the research proposed here. The book is intended for readers interested in Japanese politics, comparative welfare states, or policy for the elderly.

ProjectTitle: Post-Doctoral Fellowships in Middle Eastern Archaeology

ProjectDesc: The W. F. Albright Institute is applying for one twelve-month and one six-month post-doctoral fellowship for each of the academic years 2006-7, 2007-08, 2008-09. These would be continuous, residential fellowships at the Institute, which is located in Jerusalem. Fellows are expected to pursue a senior level research project, give a public lecture to the academic community while in residence at the Albright, and participate in the activities of the Institute's scholarly community. The fellows' research projects should culminate in scholarly publication. The Albright is dedicated to pursuing research across the entire gamut of ancient Near Eastern Studies, from pre-history through the early Islamic Period. The impact of this research transmitted through its hundreds of alumni to institutions all over the world, has had a profound effect on our understanding of the growth of western civilization and its origins in the ancient Near East.
ToSupport: One and one-half full-year humanities fellowships, for one year.

ProjectTitle: NEH Research Fellows at the Medici Project
Program: Fellowship Programs at Independent Research Institutions
ProjectDesc: The Medici Archive Project is an American Research Institution that carries out scholarly activities in the National Archive in Florence, Italy (Archivio di Stato di Firenze). These activities include the creation of the first computerized access to the Archive of the Medici Grand Dukes of Tuscany (1537-1743). Part of MAP's mission is to train emerging scholars in the values and methods of archival research in the context of an ongoing Fellowship Program, giving them the opportunity to make such research an integral part of their scholarly careers. Funding is thus sought for two NEH Research Fellows who will come to MAP for three years each (from September 2006 through August 2009 and September 2007 through August 2010). In the course of their three years with MAP, Fellows spend 20 months collaborating with MAP's research team onsite in the Florentine National Archive and the remaining time (16 months) carrying out independent research on a proposed topic of their choice. After the conclusion of their fellowships, Project Alumnae pursue scholarly careers, bringing their enhanced knowledge and expertise to universities, museums and research institutions around the world.
ToSupport: One three-year humanities fellowship.

In its approach, the study attempts to bridge the divergent perspectives of traditional philology and cognitive linguistics. ProjectTitle: Under the Tonto Rim: Conflict, Culture, and Memory in a Western Region
ProjectDesc: *Under the Tonto Rim* analyzes a core sample of a cultural identity that emerged in the rural West between 1880 and 1930. In Arizona's Rim Country, "settler culture" emerged from efforts to create community in the aftermath of ethnic, religious, and class conflicts of the 1880s. In the 1890s, settlers were challenged by new "immigrants": Tonto Apaches who abandoned the reservation and returned to their homeland. How Tontos participated in settler culture despite being relegated to the status of a lower caste is one of the book's central themes. Finally, I seek to understand how Zane Grey interpreted and legitimized settler culture in his fiction, and how that fiction resonated with readers concerned about shifting gender codes and ethnic tensions in the 1920s.

ProjectTitle: Theater and the Commercialization of Culture in France and the Colonies, 1680-1789
ProjectDesc: Between 1680 and 1789, at least seventy French cities inaugurated their first municipal playhouse, and more than a dozen engaged resident theater companies. I address why and how this investment in cultural life took place, as well as the consequences for audiences, governing elites, and actors. The successful expansion of theater outside of Paris, I argue, involved a transition from a culture of patronage to a modern commercial culture.
