ProjectTitle: Afropop Worldwide
ToSupport: Production of 26 original programs for a weekly radio program that explores the music cultures of Africa and the African Diaspora throughout the Americas, the Caribbean, and the Middle East.

ProjectTitle: Civil War Sesquicentennial Project
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultation to develop collaborative museum interpretations, traveling exhibitions, educational programs, a website, and publications about the legacy of the Civil War.

ProjectTitle: In the Shadow of Little Rock: The Life of Daisy Bates
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars on a one-hour film chronicling the life and contributions of civil rights activist Daisy Bates, 1914-99.

ProjectTitle: Reinterpretation of Collection and Exhibits
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultation to develop a new interpretive framework, collection plan, and preliminary reinstallation design about the history and culture of Edisto Island, South Carolina.

ProjectTitle: Speaking of Faith: Biographical Series
ToSupport: Production of a series of four one-hour programs, together with companion websites, profiling influential figures in American cultural and religious history for the radio series "Speaking of Faith."
Participants: Marge Osthroushko [Project Director]; Kate Moos [Project Director]; Colleen Scheck [Project Director]; Kristen Wesloh [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: American Routes: Routes to Genius
ToSupport: Production of eight two-hour topical programs and 12 documentary features as elements of an ongoing radio program that presents and interprets American vernacular music as an expression of America's varied cultures and their histories.

ProjectTitle: American Voices, from the Writers' Project
Program: Humanities Projects in Libraries and Archives
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars, librarians, and other programmers to design viewing and discussion programs with a companion website about the themes found in an NEH-supported film currently at the scripting phase, "American Voices, from the Writers' Project."
Participants: Andrea Kalin [Project Director]; Andrea Kalin [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: The Man with Six Heads: The Life and Times of Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord
ProjectDesc: The Man With Six Heads tells the highly dramatic story of the fall of the ancien regime of France, the French Revolution, the rise of Napoleon and the emergence of modern Europe through the life and adventures of Charles-Maurice Talleyrand, the foremost diplomat of his time. Talleyrand served six different regimes and participated in every major political event that occurred in France during the turbulent period between 1780-1815. Although hated by many as corrupt and amoral, Talleyrand was a visionary who tried to create a liberal, modern Europe, with France at the center, where trade replaced conquest and peace reigned between nations.
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars to develop Part One of a two-part television documentary chronicling the life and times of Charles-Maurice de Talleyrand-Périgord (1754-1832).
Participants: Richard Wormser [Project Director]; Richard Wormser [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Discovering Frankenstein
ProjectDesc: Nearly 200 years ago, teenager Mary Shelley wrote what would become one of the most famous works of literature: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus. The chilling story of Victor Frankenstein and the nameless creature he fashioned in his "workshop of filthy creation" inspired numerous plays and films, and continues to captivate the human imagination. Filmmaker Margaret Koval, in partnerhsip with OPB, proposes "Discovering Frankenstein," a two-hour national prime-time PBS documentary that will revisit Shelley's tale, exploring the era of sweeping political and social change in which she wrote. It will reveal the power of literature to express and shape our ideas about politics, science, society - and our own humanity.
ToSupport: Consultation on a two-hour film examining Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein (1818) and the evolution of the Frankenstein story in popular culture.

ProjectTitle: The Last Soviet Children: Russia's Pepsi Generation
ProjectDesc: The last generation of Soviet children taught to adore “Grandfather Lenin” was just coming of age when the USSR collapsed and their world changed beyond recognition -- in ways both liberating and disorienting. Seemingly overnight, the official messages they had heard their entire lives were swept away and replaced by their polar opposites. “The Last Soviet Children: Russia's Pepsi Generation” will be a one-hour documentary intended for national and international public television and for use in schools. During the NEH consultation period, broad humanities themes will be further developed through close work with scholars and extensive research on the issues that faced these young individuals caught in a unique moment of historical change.
ToSupport: Consultation for a one-hour television documentary that would examine how Russians experienced the social, political, and economic changes that accompanied the fall of communism in the 1980s.

ProjectTitle: Shaping the 20th Century: The Lives and Work of Charles and Ray Eames
ProjectDesc: Shaping the 20th Century: The Lives and Work of Charles and Ray Eames is a program for PBS on the eclectic American design giants. The husband and wife team of Charles and Ray Eames made its mark on architecture, furniture design, film, exhibitions, multimedia and more. They are called the most important American designers of the 20th century and their influence on the visual vernacular of the modern era is immeasurable. This program will tell their story in the context of their interesting times. More importantly, the documentary will engage the ideas that animated their work - ideas about quality, the relationship between work and play, and the power of good design and effective communication to improve individual lives and society.
ToSupport: Consultation with filmmakers and scholars for a television documentary on American industrial designers Charles and Ray Eames and their impact on visual vernacular culture in 20th-century America.

ProjectTitle: Documentary Film Daniel Burnham
ProjectDesc: American cities in the late 19c were chaotic, exploding with growth and change as the economy shifted from an agrarian to an industrial basis. In the midst of these forces was architect and urbanist Daniel Burnham whose powerful vision of what a civilized American city could be in a democratic society would transform Chicago and cities across our country. His ideas provided a model for Americans to make sense of the world around them at a critical point in our nation's history. Burnham's legacy is fascinating and complex.We seek the NEH's support to develop key humanities issues for a two-part PBS documentary about the life and work of an enormously influential but often misunderstood American cultural leader, architect Daniel Burnham.
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars on a two-hour television documentary on the life and work of American architect Daniel Burnham (1846-1912).
Participants: Judith McBrien [Project Director]; Judith McBrien [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Rose Hill Interpretive Planning
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultation to plan a revised site interpretation covering two 19th-century houses in Geneva, New York, to emphasize agricultural and social history.

ProjectTitle: The Unending Dream: The Tale of Genji in the World
ProjectDesc: We propose a TV documentary introducing the 1000-year-old Japanese novel, The Tale of Genji, and its long history of inspiring writers, artists, and performers in Japan and elsewhere. The Genji is the national literary classic of Japan; its influence over Japanese culture has persisted since it appeared. Of late, The Tale of Genji has gone increasingly international, as adaptations and evocations of the story appear in the West. These include a full-length opera, a program-length dance created by a New York Company, and an American novel in the form of an imagined memoir, as if written by the Genji's author, Murasaki Shikubu. It is time to fully introduce this great work to the West to narrow the gap that remains between the West and Asia.
ToSupport: Consultation on a one-hour television documentary about the 1,000-year-old Japanese novel, "The Tale of Genji," and artists who use the novel as a source for current work.

ProjectTitle: An Imperfect Revolution
ProjectDesc: American RadioWorks requests $65,000 to support development of An Imperfect Revolution, a one-hour public radio documentary and Web site chronicling American school desegregation in the early 1970s. American schools were the central battle-ground in the fight to end Jim Crow because African Americans knew better schools held the key to upward mobility and full acceptance into American society. Despite significant desegregation since Brown, in the past ten years African American and Latino children have increasingly wound up in racially isolated, impoverished schools. ARW will document the struggle to desegrate the nation’s schools, which had a profound effect on American race relations in the rest of the 20th century.
ToSupport: Development of a one-hour radio documentary and companion website and production of a pilot segment examining efforts to desegregate schools in six American cities in the 1970s.

ProjectTitle: Science and the Search for Meaning in the 21st Century
ProjectDesc: "Science and the Search for Meaning in the 21st Century" is a ten-part documentary series for public radio that explores the dynamic boundary between science and the humanities, through the voices of some of today's most thoughtful and articulate scholars and scientists. From stem cells, to “evil-doers,” from the environmental crisis to evolution, scientists are assembling a portrait of humanity startlingly different from the comfortable certainties about who we are, and what we ought to be. "Science and the Search for Meaning," from SoundVision Productions, draws on the ideas, approaches and resources of the humanities to explore the cutting edge of contemporary science and ask, what does it mean?
ToSupport: Development of four program treatments and a companion website for a ten-hour documentary radio series exploring how thinking in the sciences has challenged and also been challenged by thinking in fields of the humanities regarding human nature and the human condition.

ProjectTitle: Becoming American: The Literature and Film of Immigration
Program: Humanities Projects in Libraries and Archives
ProjectDesc: National Book Foundation, working with scholars of U.S. immigration and humanities related institutions, requests a consultation grant to to develop a national project based in printed literature, film, video, audiobooks, web, and other media about changing patterns of immigration to the United States and how they have helped the country develop. The project will use these consultations to understand the possible scope of the subject matter, participation of various institutions across the United States, and methods, modes and venues for dissemination.
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars, representatives from national organizations, and educational programmers about the changing patterns of immigration to the United States.
Participants: Harold Augenbraum [Project Director]; Harold Augenbraum [Project Director]

Institution: National Cowboy and Western Heritage Museum
ProjectTitle: The Nez Perce in Indian Territory
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultation for an exhibition and publication on the history of the exiled Nez Perce and their allies in Kansas and Oklahoma from 1877 to 1885.

ProjectTitle: The Lightkeepers: Illuminating History at the North Point Lighthouse
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultation to plan a revised historic site tour plus exhibits and public programs about the lighthouse that guided generations of immigrants into the port of Milwaukee between 1855 and 1930.

ProjectTitle: Site Interpretation for Tipton-Haynes
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultation to plan a permanent exhibition about the history of an East Tennessee farm complex from prehistory through Reconstruction.

ProjectTitle: Grant/Lee Exhibition
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ToSupport: Consultant to develop two complementary traveling exhibitions, one concerning Lee, the other focusing on Grant, and accompanying publications and public and school programs.

ProjectTitle: Identifying Themes for the Yellowstone National Park Segment of the Nez Perce National Historical Trail
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ProjectDesc: The only media for the 1877 Nez Perce Trail transecting Yellowstone are three, outdated mid-20th century signs; no interpretive themes have been developed. The media misrepresents the Nez Perce, omits information about their pre-1877 association with the Park, and inadvertently reinforces the impression that the Park was an uninhabited wilderness. Yellowstone Park Foundation is requesting funds to underwrite a two-day meeting at which 10 scholars, including those of Nez Perce ancestry, will identify interpretive themes, to be illuminated through media, so that millions of visitors will have the opportunity, where none exists now, to critically examine the complex facets associated with the Nez Perce Trail in Yellowstone.
ToSupport: Consultation for interpretive stations and signage about the route of the Nez Perce through the park in 1877, as well as general information about their prior presence in and use of the area.

ProjectTitle: Weathering the Years: A History of Winter in the Northern Rockies
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ProjectDesc: The Museum of the Rockies will convene and consult with an advisory group and visit other regional museums in preparation for a long-term and traveling exhibition entitled, “Weathering the Years: The History of Winter in the Northern Rockies,” to commemorate the museum’s fiftieth anniversary in 2007. The exhibition will explore winter’s role in shaping a sense of place, tying together the region’s natural and cultural histories from the nineteenth century to the present. This project will contribute to American Western scholarship and provide the public with an accessible, informative and engaging exhibition that will offer deep insights into a place with dramatic winter weather and rich and diverse cultural traditions.
ToSupport: Consultation to develop an interpretive exhibition, with school and public programs, to observe the museum's 50th anniversary by exploring how winter shapes a sense of place in the region.

ProjectTitle: Iconoclasm in Africa
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ProjectDesc: This major traveling exhibition will contrast African art, which is often made NOT to last, with the Western belief that much of art's importance comes from its permanence and its triumph over time. The Museum for African Art proposes to convene a meeting of consulting scholars to clarify the exhibition's themes and to discuss the best ways to present and interpret them to the general public. Preliminary audience evaluations will then be conducted to assess the effectiveness of the project team's conclusions.
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars and interpretive specialists to develop a traveling exhibition and catalog about the reasons that some African art forms are designed to be ephemeral or are intentionally destroyed.

ProjectTitle: Rochester: A Place of Innovation
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ProjectDesc: The Rochester Museum & Science Center requests consultation funding in the amount of $10,000 to develop a set of guiding concepts for a new exhibit about the history of invention and innovation in the Rochester region. This exhibit will constitute the centerpiece of a multidisciplinary experience that explores and explains locally developed technologies and also places them in an economic and cultural context. The consultation will bring together museum project staff, an exhibit development consultant, and three visiting scholars. It will also enable museum staff to meet with Invention at Play exhibit developers at the Smithsonian Institution.
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars and an exhibit developer to define the interpretive outline of an exhibition on the history of invention and innovation in Rochester.

ProjectTitle: York: Crossroads of the American Revolution, 1775-1783
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ProjectDesc: YCHT will hire three humanities scholars to aid in the development of the intellectual and educational content for a reinterpretation of its Colonial Complex (3 historic sites/1 replica). The plan will upgrade traditional interpretative programming (guided tours, etc.) and integrate living history techniques into the visitor experience. YCHT has chosen the “York: Crossroads of the American Revolution” theme because: 1) Little research has been done on the impact of the War in the hinterland; and 2) York, PA, from 1775 to 1783, was a center of Revolutionary activity, supplying men/staples to the Continental Army, housing prisoners of war, and serving as provisional capital to the Continental Congress from September 30, 1777 to June 27, 1778.
ToSupport: Consultation with scholars to plan for a reinterpretation of a colonial complex in York, Pennsylvania, with special focus on the changes that occurred in the area as a result of the American Revolution.

ProjectTitle: The Artist Behind the Work: A New Installation of NW Coast Native Art from the Seattle Art Museum's Permanent Collection
Program: Humanities Projects in Museums and Historical Organizations
ProjectDesc: The permanent exhibition of the Seattle Art Museum's superb collection of Northwest Coast Native art will be completely renewed as part of an overall museum expansion. The new installation will enact the theme of the individual artist, their influences and lasting legacies -- "The Artist Behind the Work." The underlying premise to explicate the works of individual artists will be from the point of view of the maker and original audience, as well as from historical viewpoints, thus demonstrating the changing meanings of the artwork over time and through differing cultural lenses.
ToSupport: Consultation to plan a reinstallation of the museum's permanent exhibition of Northwest Coast Native art.

ProjectTitle: Natural Law, Natural Rights, and the American Constitution
ProjectDesc: The Witherspoon Institute proposes to organize a series of university faculty workshops on “The Natural Law Foundations of the American Constitution” for faculty members involved in the James Madison Program in American Ideals and Institutions at Princeton University, the Core Humanities Program at Villanova University, and Seton Hall University. The goal is to provide faculty members with a forum in which they can explore natural law thinking in depth, including the critical role it played in the foundation of the American republic’s Founding debate. Participants will be challenged to think about new ways in which traditional and contemporary natural law theory bolsters and illuminates modern democratic theory.
ToSupport: A series of workshops for faculty and visiting fellows at Seton Hall University, Villanova University, and Princeton University on the natural law foundations of the American constitution.

ProjectTitle: Visions of Slavery and Freedom in the Writings of Lydia Maria Child, Frederick Douglass, Herman Melville and Harriet Jacobs
ProjectDesc: This project will offer a series of interdisciplinary presentations, workshops and field trips to twenty-five teachers of History, Social Studies, American Literature and English Language Arts frm public, parochial and charter schools in southeastern Massachusetts, Cape Cod and Nantucket. We will meet once a month from January to May 2006 and again for an intensive four-day session in June 2006 to study the roles these four antebellum authors played in the "evolution of the concepts of personal freedom, individual responsibility and respect for human dignity" as described in the Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Frameworks.
ToSupport: A faculty humanities workshop for twenty-five school teachers on visions of slavery and freedom in the writings of Lydia Maria Child, Frederick Douglass, Herman Melville, and Harriet Jacobs.

Institution: Theatre for a New Audience, Inc.
ProjectTitle: Shakespeare Teachers' Workshop
ProjectDesc: Theatre for a New Audience is implementing a pilot program – the Shakespeare Teachers’ Workshop – an intensive professional development program focusing on Shakespeare, consisting of a two-week summer seminar and two one-day weekend workshops in the fall and spring, developed for public and private school teachers in the New York City area. Led by Columbia University professors David Scott Kastan and James S. Shapiro, the workshop will provide 16 teachers with advanced skills to identify and understand the language, themes and context of Shakespearean plays. In the first year of the program, participants will study The Winter’s Tale (a romance), Othello (a tragedy), and Much Ado About Nothing (a comedy).
ToSupport: An intensive two-week summer program followed by weekend workshops in fall and spring on The Winter's Tale, Othello, and Much Ado About Nothing for sixteen New York City public and private school teachers in grades 5-12.

Institution: George C. Wallace State Community College
ProjectTitle: Alabama Storytellers and Myths: A Legacy of Lore
ProjectDesc: Wallace Community College proposes a series of faculty workshops to study the influence and impact of Alabama myths and stories on the curricula at the College. The primary goal of the workshops is to enrich the participants’ understanding of the wisdom and power found in myths and stories so that they will draw from Alabama’s rich sources of lore to teach their students, to reinvent their classes relevant to the lives and times of their students, to reach out to their colleagues, and to remind themselves of their own unique stories.
ToSupport: A series of interdisciplinary faculty workshops on the "mythology" of the South and the role of Alabama writers in contributing to such a mythology.

ProjectTitle: Learning and Teaching Asian Culture through Theater: Interdisciplinary Humanities Workshop Series on Asian Theater
ProjectDesc: The project focuses on the interdisciplinary study of classical Asian theaters as a unique avenue through which to gain an intimate understanding of Asian culture and history. Two weekend workshops are designed to build basic knowledge of Asian theater and encourage participants to incorporate Asian theater studies in their curricular offerings at two- and four-year undergraduate institutions. It aims to provide a high-quality intellecutal program for undergraduate teaching faculty in the Southwestern region of the United States who would like to expand their intellectual horizen by incorporating signficant Asian contents in their humanities courses.
ToSupport: Two three-day workshops for twenty-five undergraduate faculty in Asian theater, focusing on Japanese, Indonesian, and Indian dramatic traditions.

ProjectTitle: Teaching World History: Comparisons and Connections
ProjectDesc: Teaching Global History will provide a workshop in World History for 20 K-12 teachers in northwest and north central Wisconsin. Teachers will work with project faculty to focus on major comparative themes in World history as they master content knowledge, read and discuss recent scholarship and develop standards-based lessons using on primary sources that they select.
ToSupport: A workshop in world history for twenty K-12 teachers in northwest Wisconsin, to be held on six weekends and one week in the summer during 2005-2006.

ProjectTitle: Winning the Vote: The Women's Suffrage Movement in the United States
ProjectDesc: Central Michigan University and the Michigan Women’s Historical Center propose a professional development workshop for social studies teachers on the history of the women’s suffrage movement. In a five day summer workshop and three days of follow up, we will discuss the history of the movement. This workshop will address the topic through readings of primary sources drawn from the time , through examination of artifacts, and in discussions led by scholars who specialize in this movement. In addition, music from the time, documentaries, and dramatic portrayals will add to the seminar. Each teacher participant will be required to work on an individual project that will then be used as part of a traveling exhibition created by the group.
ToSupport: A five-day workshop for Michigan social studies teachers that would examine the history of the women's suffrage movement in the United States.

ProjectTitle: The Examined Life: Hellenic Studies in the Schools
ProjectDesc: "The Examined Life" is an educational program that aims to strengthen the humanities curriculum in the southern New Jersey schools through Hellenic studies seminars, workshops, and ongoing discussions of ways to integrate knowledge and teaching. The overarching theme is the Socratic call to Know Thyself (gnothi s'auton). Asking participants to explore what it means to be human through the lens of Greek antiquity, the "Examined Life" program taps into the great reservoir of Greek thought and culture and its power to transform student minds.
ToSupport: A series of workshop for twenty New Jersey teachers and administrators to explore the meaning of the human experience through reading and discussion of ancient Greek literature and history.

ProjectTitle: Reading Narratives in Four Religious Traditions
ToSupport: A yearlong, six-seminar workshop for eighteen school teachers in the mid-Hudson region of New York on father/son narratives in Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism.

ProjectTitle: Neoclassicism in Europe and North America, 1750-1825
ToSupport: A two-week summer workshop for sixteen Southern California high school teachers on European and North American neoclassicism in the period 1750 to 1825, to be held at the Huntington Library.

ProjectTitle: The Circle of We: The Expanding Definition of American Citizenship
ToSupport: Five workshops for Miami-Dade County teachers examining the ways that American citizenship has been defined and expanded in the eighteenth, nineteenth, and twentieth centuries.

ProjectTitle: African Americans and the Mills and Mill Villages of Gaston County
ToSupport: A series of workshops for fifteen college and school teachers on the African American experience in the textile mills of rural North Carolina.

ProjectTitle: Cultural Encounters in Global Contexts: Teaching World Literature in General Education English Courses
ToSupport: A yearlong project to enable sixteen faculty members at eight geographically-dispersed institutions to study with leading scholars to improve the teaching of world literature texts.

ProjectTitle: Battling for Survival: American Indians in Montana
ToSupport: Two five-day workshops for forty Montana K-12 teachers on Northern Cheyenne history and contemporary Cheyenne Indian culture.

ProjectTitle: The Humanities in Latin American and Caribbean Studies
ToSupport: A twelve-session workshop for social studies and foreign language teachers that would examine the history, literature, and cultures of Latin America and the Caribbean.

ProjectTitle: Socratic Questions
ToSupport: A series of faculty development workshops that place Socratic questions and methods into dialogue with core texts in the two-semester course sequence on western civilization required of all first-year students.
Participants: Peter Busch [Project Director]; Marylu Hill [Co Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Africa and the Americas
ToSupport: A series of workshops for faculty at four colleges to study the relationships between the literatures of post-colonial Africa and the African Diasporas of the Caribbean and the United States.

ProjectTitle: 2005 Jefferson Lecture: "In Defense of History"
ToSupport: No to support statement

ProjectTitle: Alaska's March to Statehood: Celebrating the Constitution
ProjectDesc: The year 2009 marks the 50th Anniversary of Alaska Statehood. A landmark event preceeding Statehood was the Alaska Constitutional Convention. It spanned 76 days from November 8, 1955 until February 6, 1956. Plans to celebrate this landmark occasion are cropping up across the state. Through the 2005 We The People Initiative, the Alaska Humanities Forum aims to insure that these celebrations enjoy rich historical content in many formats, targeting Alaskans of all ages.
ToSupport: Projects that mark the 50th Anniversary of Alaska statehood including the Alaska Constitutional Convention Almanac Radio Broadcast series, a convention for high-school and college students and a re-grant program.
Participants: Ira Perman [Project Director]; Gregory Kimura [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: WTP in Arizona 2005-2006
ProjectDesc: AHC will present five projects in 2005-2006 under the auspices of the We the People initiative. These projects will promote the teaching of American history and give Arizona residents a broader perspective on their state's history. The projects will be a Cesar Chavez traveling exhibit created and toured in cooperation with Humanities Texas, the traveling exhibit Between Fences through Museum on Main Street, Motheread's My United States family literacy/citizenship curriculum, a one-day History Fest for high school history teachers, and cultural heritage tourism grants.
ToSupport: Projects including a traveling exhibit on the life of labor leader César Chávez, training in a family literacy/citizenship curriculum, a History fest for high school teachers and cultural heritage tourism grants.

ProjectTitle: New Californians Exhibition
ProjectDesc: The New Californians Exhibition builds on the success of five projects conducted during the California Council for the Humanities' 2005 California Stories Uncovered campaign. Immigrant youth from countries ranging from Russia to the Republic of the Congo worked with award-winning photographers and writing instructors to create 5 exhibits in communities ranging from the San Francisco Bay Area to Orange County. The Exhibition program will be a collaboration between the Council and other cultural institutions to expand these efforts and bring them to new communities and audiences statewide.
ToSupport: A traveling exhibition in eight locations over two years, together with local programming and documentary projects in the host communities, focused on the experiences of new immigrant groups to California, with special emphasis on young people.
Participants: Ralph Lewin [Project Director]; Christina Sutherland [Project Director]; Julie Fry [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Freedom's Fathers: Connecting People, Cultures and Ideas
ProjectDesc: Freedom's Fathers is a multi-faceted program focusing on the dramatic story behind the development of the United States Constitution. The audience participants will be mostly citizens older than 18. Of particular interest will be how the octogenarian Ben Franklin, youthful James Madison, and the battle - weary George Washington helped to shape the thinking that led to this " miracle in Philadelphia". Delaware, the state that started a nation, was represented by five delegates- John Dickinson, Gunning Bedford, George Reed, Richard Bassett and Jacob Broom.
ToSupport: A series of public programs, including Chautauqua presentations and symposia, on the history and principles of the US Constitution, with emphasis on the contributions of Delaware citizens to the drafting of the document, followed by visits to the US Constitution Center in Philadelphia.

ProjectTitle: Extending the Circle of We: Democracy and Diversity in the Sunshine State
ProjectDesc: One of our nation’s most remarkable achievements has been its extension of democratic rights and citizenship to diverse groups of people. From the Constitutional Convention, to women’s suffrage and civil rights, to immigrants seeking both economic opportunity and refuge, the range of people included in “We the People” has been consistently debated and redefined. This proposal outlines five weeklong teachers seminars. These seminars will explore various aspects of Florida’s cultural diversity and the historic events, people, values and institutions that have shaped our multicultural identity.
ToSupport: Five week-long teacher seminars exploring various aspects of Florida's cultural diversity and the historic events, people, values, and institutions that have shaped the state's multicultural identity.

ProjectTitle: We the People in Georgia 2005
ProjectDesc: Through “We the People in Georgia, 2005”, the Georgia Humanities Council will distribute a poster/history timeline to teachers that highlights the New Georgia Encyclopedia and the Digital Library of Georgia, two electronic resources. The Council will also strengthen its National History Day in Georgia program (which has the theme “Taking a Stand in History” for 2006) through the development of materials and through outreach at conferences and workshops. Additionally, the Council will support public programs through regrants, in order to reach adult community members.
ToSupport: Distribution of a poster/history timeline to teachers, strengthening of the National History Day in Georgia program, the 2006 theme of which is "Taking a Stand in History," and a regrant program targeted to adults.

ProjectTitle: Guampedia: Religion's Role in Guam's History
ProjectDesc: The Guam Humanities Council has recently begun creating an online encyclopedia about Guam. "Guampedia" has 18 subject rubrics with topics such as ancient history of the Chamorro people, culture and religion. We propose to use this grant to produce the religion rubric. We will include photographs, historical drawings and audio and video when available. An outline is at www.guampedia.com/browse subjects. Click on "Religion." View a sample entry: "FR. ROMAN MARIA DE VERA: Pioneer Promoter of the Chamorro Language."
ToSupport: Development of section on Chamorro religious practices for the online encyclopedia about Guam, "Guampedia," with photographs, historical drawings, and, when available, audio and video, and development of guides to help teachers use this material.

ProjectTitle: Produce for Victory: World War II and the Home Front in America and in Hawai'i
ProjectDesc: The Hawai’i Council for the Humanities will tour a Smithsonian Institution Museum on Main Street exhibition called “Produce for Victory: Posters on the American Home Front, 1941-1945” to seven community venues around the state in 2006. Each site will develop local programs through mini-grants provided by HCH and the Council will coordinate development of a display and curriculum materials and hold a teacher workshop on the significance of World War II and the home front around the nation, including the immediate post-war period, and compare and contrast this with the experience in Hawai‘i.
ToSupport: A traveling exhibition, "Produce for Victory: Posters on the American Home Front, 1941-1945" in seven communities throughout the state, together with local programming and a teacher workshop on the significance of World War II.

ProjectTitle: Prime Time Family Reading and Chautauqua in Schools
ProjectDesc: Kentucky Humanities Council requests $42,530 for Prime Time Family Reading Time and $26,550 for Kentucky Chautauqua in our schools. KHC is currently conducting 7 Prime Time programs in partnership with the Kentucky Dept. for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), which is conducting 4 programs. Our request would enable KHC to support Prime Time in 6 libraries (KDLA will support 4 more) for a second year, develop our own team of trainers, and establish a track record on which to base future funding requests. Our Chautauqua joins those of other councils as a proven vehicle for teaching American history.
ToSupport: To support the Prime Time Family Reading Time program in six libraries for a second year, and, working with the coordinators of the Teaching American History grants, to provide sixty Chautauqua programs to schools in five regions of Kentucky.
Participants: Virginia Carter [Project Director]; Albert Chandler [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: From Colony to Commonwealth: The Northern Mariana Islands and the "American Century"
ProjectDesc: This program comprises four projects that will examine the shared history of the Northern Mariana Islands (NMI) and the United States during the 100 year period (ca. 1898-1999) some historians refer to as the “American Century” and how this shared history has shaped the social, cultural, economic, and political life in the NMI today. These projects include: American Foreign Policy; Guam-NMI Relations; the Road to Commonwealth; and Constitutional Awareness. All will be open to the public on Saipan, Tinian, and Rota including students from elementary school to college.
ToSupport: Chautauqua performances, lectures, seminars, symposia, classroom activities and technology projects on the period 1898-1999 to increase awareness of the shared history of the Northern Mariana Islands and the United States, foster understanding of the documents that define the Commonwealth and explore current issues related to democratic principles.
Participants: Herman Guerrero [Project Director]; Debra Cabrera [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: The People of Mississippi: We Are America
ProjectDesc: As the US settles into a new century and millennium, shaken by strife at home and violent conflict abroad, with a population divided on basic values and core beliefs, thoughtful citizens are considering anew our country, its past, its goals for the future. The MHC requests WTP funds for print, radio, and Internet programs on MS history and culture along with analysis and insight as basis for reflection and discussion. These projects draw on and enlarge current programs and expand collaborations with other partners.
ToSupport: Continuation of "Mississippi Moments," a series of 4-minute radio segments, development of an online Mississippi timeline, and revision and updating of a 1992 publication, Ethnic Heritage in Mississippi.

ProjectTitle: We The People in Montana, 2005-2006
ProjectDesc: The Montana Committee for the Humanities proposes using FY2005 We The People grant funds in 2005 and 2006 to support a major statewide conference on Montana history and culture and a variety of American history and culture projects through its on-going Speakers Bureau, regrants program, OpenBook reading and discussion program, and its annual Montana Festival of the Book.
ToSupport: A statewide conference on Montana history and culture, and a variety of American history and culture projects through the Committee's speakers bureau, grants program, reading and discussion groups, and the annual Montana Festival of the Book.
Participants: Kim Anderson [Project Director]; Kenneth Egan [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: North Dakota Reads
ProjectDesc: The NDHC requests funding for “North Dakota Reads,” a reading and discussion program led by scholars throughout the state.Through directed conversations, the NDHC will develop themes and choose books for the pre-packaged programs, each one with a scholar assigned to serve as a resource and facilitator. Using a printed and on-line catalog and extensive publicity through its partners, the NDHC will loan books and provide discussion leaders to groups. “North Dakota Reads” will celebrate reading and cultural understanding in a book festival, bringing writers together with readers of all ages.
ToSupport: "North Dakota Reads," a reading and discussion program using scholar-facilitators, printed and online catalogues, and a book loan program, culminating in a book festival.
Participants: Janet Daley Jury [Project Director]; Brenna Gerhardt [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: We The People--Nebraska
ProjectDesc: The Nebraska Humanities Council (NHC) requests $55,380 in We The People funding to support three programs: $18,420 to help underwrite the Great Plains Chautauqua, "From Sea to Shining Sea: American Expansion and Cultural Change, 1790-1850" in Alliance and Albion, Nebraska during the summer of 2006; $13,235 to help fund the 2005-2006 Capitol Forum, a curriculum-based program to encourage 1500 Nebraska high school students to better understand American democratic values; and $18,725 to support speakers on U.S. and Great Plains history from the Council's Humanities Resource Center.

ProjectTitle: Suicide in the Early American South
ProjectDesc: The proposed project is a history of suicide in the early American South from the colonial period through the Civil War. During these years, suicide was a recurring theme in public, private, and popular documents, but historians have paid little attention to its prevalence or significance. The American Revolution marked a dramatic change in the legal, cultural, and political meanings of suicide and the emergence of distinctively southern attitudes toward violence. My goal in this project is to analyze these various narratives of self-murder, situate them in a comparative colonial, regional, and transatlantic context, and analyze how and why the legal, cultural, and political meanings of suicide in the South change over time.

ProjectTitle: Inventing English Textuality in 15th-Century Religious Writing
ProjectDesc: Examines disparate canonizing gestures in 15th-c. religious writing, to rethink the impact of Lollardy on English reading and writing. Challenging a view of the Lollards as democratizers and their opponents as censors, argues that each side in the controversy canonized a single model of reading as uniquely authoritative. Describes alternate canonizing projects that sought to preserve the diversity and multiplicity of 14th-c. vernacular theologies, resisting the polarizing and essentializing impulses of the Lollard controversy. Analyzes the role of gender and of narrative in these competing inventions of English textuality; asks how they might complicate received narratives of the transition from medieval to Early Modern.

ProjectTitle: Cicero's Ethics
ProjectDesc: Cicero embraces the Stoic view that knowledge is a harbor from the storms of fortune, and the means to happiness. Yet he also endorses the Academics' refutation of Stoic epistemology and remains skeptical with regard to how, or even whether, knowledge is possible. Thus the main problem I address in this book: How can philosophy achieve such great things if it does not succeed in fulfilling our desire for knowledge? In answering this question, I examine Cicero's portrait of Socrates as the model of both moral and epistemic virtue. I also discuss the ways in which Cicero adopts and modifies Stoic ethics in accordance with what he sees as our epistemic limitations.

ProjectTitle: Race, Soldiering, and Transnational Citizenship in Mexican American War Narratives, 1835-2005
ProjectDesc: This study examines the complex negotiations of race and citizenship by Mexican American soldier authors from the early 19th century to the present through a critical survey of poems, letters, short stories, novels, memoirs, cinema, and popular song lyrics. These texts are undergirded by dramatic episodes in which Mexican American soldiers explore their roles as U.S. allies, or enemies, through identifications, and misidentifications, with other combatants and conflict participants. These recognition scenes variously involve xenophobic metaphors, subaltern multiracial alliances, problematic transnational identifications, regional identity claims, and post-racialist discourses that adumbrate new postnational Latina/o identities today.

ProjectTitle: A Cultural History of the Russian Home
ProjectDesc: Over the past decade or so, there has been an explosion of scholarly interest in the intimate sphere of life in Russian history. This scholarship on the private realm not only reflects a borrowing of frameworks from the West, but also allows for, and indeed forces, an interrogation of these very frameworks. "Domestic Interiors" fits squarely in this new body of scholarship. This book will explore the physical realities and the ideological imaginings of the interior space of the Russian home from the second half of the nineteenth century through the first third of the twentieth. In doing so, this project will highlight how Russia’s struggle toward modernity was manifest in changing notions about the domestic hearth.

ProjectTitle: The Creaton of Civic Identity in 16th-Century Venice
ProjectDesc: This proposal is to fund one year of salary replacement to support the completion of a book about the development of the state in early modern Europe. My book argues that a crucial but unrecognized component of statebuilding was the management of public speech and foul language. While scholars have long studied the history of language, they have done so largely by considering literary, printed texts. My study, by contrast, employs sociolinguistic concepts to examine the actual words of everyday people in the archival documents of renaissance Venice. I demonstrate that early modern states formed not only by building armies and bureaucracies, but also by imposing a normative language on their citizens and immigrants.

ProjectTitle: An Anthology of Epitaphs from the Tang Dynasty, 618-907

The emphasis will be placed on 1) women’s roles and identities; 2) women and religion; 3) practices related to gender systems; and 4) gender and Tang history. When completed, the book will provide the first collection of primary sources in English translation to focus on Chinese women during the Tang Dynasty.

ProjectTitle: Geopolitics and Geopieties in 20th-Century Nagano

I have been fortunate to identify a number of cases of women who passed from Christianity to Islam (or in the opposite direction), and never returned to their birth religions. . . . The richness of [relevant] documentary sources has allowed me to develop three detailed narratives of women who crossed early modern religious boundaries.

ProjectTitle: Biography of Elizabeth Cady Stanton, 19th-Century Feminist and Intellectual

Benefitting from new scholarship in women's history and feminist political theory, and my own scholarly engagement with questions of political identity and reform activism, this biography will use Stanton's life story as a window through which to view, and reshape, the narrative of nineteenth-century feminism and American intellectual life itself.

ProjectTitle: The Work of Attribution in the Age of Anonymous Publication
ProjectDesc: THE WORK OF ATTRIBUTION IN THE AGE OF ANONYMOUS PUBLICATION investigates how individual readers in the period and region we tend to credit with the invention of modern authorship--the eighteenth-century Anglophone Atlantic--dealt with that era’s unprecedented proliferation of anonymous and pseudonymous publications. By tracing the sustained negotiations between readers and writers over who had the authority to define an author’s oeuvre and so shape his or her reputation, this book demonstrates that the modern author function is as much the collective creation “from below” of myriad individual readers as it is the product of any of the various institutions or heroic writers to which its invention has been traditionally credited.

ProjectTitle: Chinese Medical Epistemology in Transition, ca. 350 BCE-220 CE
ProjectDesc: This study explains the origins of acupuncture during the Western Han period (206 BCE-25 CE) in terms of a shift in medical epistemology around the first century BCE. Whereas earlier medical theorists stressed knowledge about the body grounded in experience, those living after the first century BCE de-emphasized the experience of ordinary men in favor of revealed wisdom attributed to sages. This shift was related to the rise of a new, political notion of sagehood in the Qin court, which held that sages were not morally perfected men, but beings with extraordinary faculties of perception.

ProjectTitle: Atoms for Peace and Health: Tracing the Manhattan Project through Postwar Biomedicine
ProjectDesc: After World War II, the U. S. Atomic Energy Commission (AEC) began mass-producing radioisotopes, sending out nearly 64,000 shipments of radioactive materials to scientists and physicians by 1955. AEC radioisotopes provided physicians with new tools for diagnosis and therapy and equipped biologists to trace molecular transformations from metabolic pathways to ecosystems. My book will tell the story of how these radioisotopes, which were simultaneously scientific tools and political icons, transformed biomedicine.

ProjectTitle: The Reformation of Suffering: Protestants, Plague, and Misfortune in Early Modern Germany
ProjectDesc: This project examines how the Protestant Reformation sought to effect a fundamental change in the way early modern Europeans understood and coped with suffering. An essential though understudied part of the Reformation program was the rejection of the late medieval approach to suffering and the development of a new approach in its stead. This project traces the Protestant “reformation of suffering” from its origins in the thought of the major reformers to its actual reception among the common folk. The project is related to two larger themes in recent historiography: the impact of the Reformation on lay piety and popular culture in early modern Europe and the role of the Protestantism in the secularization of western civilization.

ProjectTitle: People as Pictures: Visualities in Texts and Images from the Second through Fourth Centuries CE

I aim to describe a fundamental cultural shift marking the boundary between classical and late antiquity, one which consisted in redeploying the social functions and power of vision and vesting living persons with the character and qualities of images.

ProjectTitle: Aristotle's "Exhortation to Philosophy" (Protrepticus Philosophias)

Our planned translation of 'Protrepticus', with introduction and commentary, will reintroduce the work into the Aristotelian canon, illuminate his philosophy for scholars and philosophers, and provide a welcome new tool for introducing students to Aristotle and to philosophy.

ProjectTitle: Muslims in Medieval Europe

ProjectTitle: Adam Smith and the Character of Virtue
ProjectDesc: Recent scholarship has shown that Adam Smith defended commercial society on the grounds that its material benefits outweigh its moral deficiencies. In particular, his new study of the "character of virtue," I claim, was intended to promote within modernity a recovery of the classical ethical virtues of prudence, magnanimity and beneficence, the virtues that Smith considered threatened by commercial society yet necessary for its ennoblement.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Archives
ProjectDesc: The RMC Heritage Archives wishes to contract with Idaho State Archivist Steven Walker to conduct a three-day general assessment of the Archives’ resources, resulting in a written report, and one-day training workshop. Library/Archives staff will use the report as a base for developing an archival management plan, patron use policies, and best practices for processing and cataloguing holdings. The report will include practical solutions for maximizing use of existing equipment, furniture, space, and supplies; and will provide a list of additional items deemed essential. RMC has never received NEH funds and is seeking a $5,000 grant to cover the costs of the assessment, training, and purchase of archival equipment, supplies, and furniture.
ToSupport: General preservation and archival management assessments, the purchase of supplies, and a one-day workshop for archival, manuscript, and photographic collections related to the history of Rocky Mountain College and the settlement of Montana from 1878 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Preservation and Access Assessment for the Congressional Archives
ProjectDesc: The Carl Albert Congressional Research and Studies Center at the University of Oklahoma proposes to hire a consultant to conduct a preservation needs assessment of its archival collections. The consultant will conduct on-site surveys of collections at two sites. Through visits and interviews the consultant will assess the general condition of the collections, organization, housing, security, and storage environment. The consultant will make recommendations for a long-term archival management plan that addresses storage, preservation, and access of the collections.
ToSupport: A preservation and access assessment of the Carl Albert Center's Congressional Archives that date from 1850 to 2002.

ProjectTitle: Preserving the Museum's Textile Collection
ProjectDesc: Preserving the Ella Sharp Textile Collection is a textile preservation project in which 52 Level I textile artifacts from the Museum's permanent collection are to be placed into improved collections storage according to professional practices and recommendations in a Conservation Assessment Report completed in 1993 by consultant conservator Geoffrey Brown.
ToSupport: Purchasing storage materials to rehouse a 52-item collection of 19th- and 20th-century textiles in a newly constructed storage area.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment and Workshop
ProjectDesc: With the help of a consultant, Emporia State University Libraries and Archives will undertake a preservation assessment of its archival holdings at two sites to define an optimal long-range plan for the care of its collections and present a preservation workshop based on the findings of the survey for the benefit of the institution's community of personnel and users. Unsound and deterioration environmental conditions at the storage sites threaten unique and nationally significant collections including the papers of William Allen White (1864-1944), a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist; the May Massee Collection of original artwork for over 900 children's books (1883-1966); and the Walter M. Andersen Collection of nearly 50,000 photographic images documenting the history of Kansas and US railroad history from 1860-2001. This preservation assessment will provide the institution with information pertaining to current facilities, collection care policies, and emergency preparedness.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the special collections held by the Emporia State University Libraries and Archives and a preservation training workshop for library and archival staff.

ProjectTitle: Film Collection Rehousing and Environmental Monitoring Project
ProjectDesc: Appalshop, Inc. proposes a grant for the purchase of environmental monitoring equipment and archival film supplies for its media vaults. The equipment and supplies will serve to enhance Appalshop’s archival vault development project and the long-term care and use of present and future holdings by allowing for precise measurements of the environmental conditions in the archival storage areas and by extending the life of the moving image materials that comprise the 16mm collections.
ToSupport: The purchase of an environmental monitor and related computer software and archival film supplies for six major still and moving images collections that cover life in central Appalachia since the 1930s.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of the Medical Heritage Center
ProjectDesc: Preservation Survey for the Medical Heritage Center
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the collections, facility, and preservation policies of the University's Medical Heritage Center, which focuses on the history of medicine and the health sciences.
Participants: Janet Waters [Project Director]; Lynda Hartel [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Preservation and Storage of the Institute's Historic Map Collection
ToSupport: The purchase of flat file storage cabinets and supplies for housing oversized 19th-century U.S. Coast Survey maps.

Institution: County of Essex Department of Parks, Recreation, and Cultural Affairs
ProjectTitle: Historical Maps and Plans Storage
ProjectDesc: The Essex County Park Commission was established in 1895, becoming the first county park system in the country and a prototype for other multi-municipality park developments. The Commission archive contains unique evidence of the design process behind the creation of a park, as well as a century of changes. This project focuses on the historic maps and plans which identify properties to be acquired, indicate recreation trends, or illustrate the grading, landscaping, and structural elements of the parks. In order to preserve these valuable documents, the Department will purchase flat file storage and preservation supplies for rehousing the map and plan collection of the Park Commission as recommended by a preservation assessment.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture and preservation supplies for maps, plans, and blueprints that document the development from 1895 to 1979 of a park system that has served Newark and its densely populated suburbs.

ProjectTitle: Collection Assessment and Training
ProjectDesc: We will use the grant funds to hire Terri Schindel, Conservator, to conduct training of staff and volunteers in proper storage techniques for organic materials in our collection. Her assessment of the current storage conditions will guide us in setting short-, mid-, and long-term goals for such items as staffing, collection policies, storage, exhibits, and facilities. Facility recommendations will include environmental controls, emergency preparedness and security. Area museums will be invited to send representatives to the training to enhance the training opportunity and begin dialog among museums.
ToSupport: Hiring a conservation consultant to conduct a preservation assessment of textiles, as well as to provide a training workshop for staff and volunteers of the museum. The staffs of area museums would be invited to participate in the training workshop.

ProjectTitle: Preservation of the Jericho Public Library's Local History Collection
ProjectDesc: The Jericho Public Library requests a Preservation Assistance Grant to implement our short-, medium- and long-term priorities as outlined in our Preservation Planning Survey. The Library has made significant progress toward insuring the long-term survival of the local history collection, but there are important preservation needs still to be addressed. Our goal is to meet our short -and medium-term priorities so we can focus on the long-term priorities. Our long-range plans are to make this room as archivally correct, and as secure yet as accessible as possible.
ToSupport: The purchase of light filters, a storage cabinet, and preservation supplies for books, manuscripts, archival records, photographs, and other records related to the history of Jericho, New York, from the 17th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring and Collections Storage Improvements
ProjectDesc: The USS Constellation Museum desires funding to purchase collections storage furniture, conservation materials, and environmental monitoring equipment. These materials are for use in implementing the recommendations made in the Museum’s General Conservation Assessment Report, written as part of the institution’s participation in the Conservation Assessment Program (CAP). Specifically, the Museum seeks to acquire a Viking V238 Mark IV Conservation Cabinet, with relevant interior hardware and conservation materials, to house its shipbuilding tools and crew ephemera collections. In addition, the Museum would like to purchase a hygrothermograph to monitor conditions within its collections storage area.
ToSupport: The purchase of equipment to monitor environmental conditions and cabinets to properly store collections, which include shipbuilding tools dating from the mid to late 19th century and personal artifacts owned or used by those who sailed aboard the "Constellation" during its 100 years of service from 1855 to 1955.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Works of Art on Paper
ProjectDesc: The New Jersey Historical Society (NJHS) will contract with paper conservator Caroline Rieger to conduct a general preservation assessment of a portion of our collection of approximately 1,150 works of art on paper. The project will include an item-by-item survey of the collection and a long-range plan for its care, including prioritized recommendations for preservation measures. The request of $5,000 will cover the total cost of the project, including the purchase of basic preservation supplies recommended by Ms. Rieger in her letter of commitment. This project is part of NJHS’s organizational commitment to preserve and promote New Jersey’s artistic and cultural heritage.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of 1,150 works of art on paper that relate to the history of New Jersey from the 18th century to the present, with an evaluation of the condition of each item and recommendations for prioritized measures for their preservation and for the purchase of supplies.

ProjectTitle: Costume Collection Conservation Assessment
ProjectDesc: The James Monroe Museum and Memorial Library wishes to begin the process of conserving its 55-piece costume collection, in the hopes of making it available to the public for interpretation and study. We would like to begin this process with the hiring of a costume conservation specialist to assess the collection. This specialist will examine each item in the costume collection, assess its stability or state of deterioration, prioritize items for future conservation and advise the staff on a plan for the long-term care of the collection.
ToSupport: Hiring a curatorial consultant and a conservator to conduct a preservation assessment of a 55-piece clothing collection that belonged to President James Monroe and his family. The consultants would develop a conservation treatment plan for each item and recommend appropriate storage and handling guidelines for the collection.

ProjectTitle: Consultation and Training Workshop for the T. J. Collins Architectural Drawing Collection
ProjectDesc: This project will help preserve the T. J. Collins Architectural Collection by providing hands-on training to staff and select volunteers in proper conservation treatment methods for the historic architectural drawings. This significant collection spans nearly 100 years of architectural design, from T. J. Collins' initial work in the early 1890s, through his sons' and grandson's work through the mid-20th century. The Conservation Center for Art and Historic Artifacts will provide a professional paper conservator to instruct Historic Staunton Foundation staff and volunteers in proper material identification and conservation treatment to accomplish Priority 1 (surface cleaning and flattening) as recommended in their 2005 Conservation Survey.
ToSupport: A workshop to train the staff and volunteers of an organization dedicated to the preservation of historic buildings in the care of architectural drawings and the creation of a guide to collection care by the consultant who conducts the workshop.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Humanities Collection
ProjectDesc: University Libraries (UL) serves the teaching and research needs of 35,000 undergraduates and graduate students, as well as 14,000 faculty and staff at the University of Cincinnati. While UL has made every effort to preserve and conserve the on-site collection (1.7 million volumes), the pace of collection growth has outpaced the level of staff available to effectively monitor, mend, and assess the collection. In order to improve and stabilize the condition of our existing collection and prepare for future collections, UL would like to hire a preservation consultant to assess the on-site humanities collection and facilities and develop a simple, clear preservation plan that focuses on processes and future directions.
ToSupport: The hiring of a consultant to conduct a preservation assessment of the humanities collections and facilities in the libraries of the University of Cincinnati.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Marymount Manhattan College Archives
ProjectDesc: MMC seeks funding to: 1. Analyze space needs and make projections for the next 15-20 years; 2. Analyze patron use and recommend measures to secure the collection and provide workspace; 3. Assess fire, heat, humidity, light, pest and theft risks; 4. Prepare a disaster plan; 5. Make recommendations for the reformatting of the archive’s audiovisual materials; 6. Make recommendations regarding the storage and cataloguing of the archive’s collection of three-dimensional objects; 7. Assess the finding guides for their conversion to electronic formats accessible via the Internet; 8. Assess staff needs and training; 9. Create a finding guide template for the archivist; 10. Identify ways to incorporate the archive into the curriculum.
ToSupport: An assessment of the disaster response, security, and facility needs of the archive as well as the preservation and management of textual, audiovisual, and photographic records related to the college's institutional history and to former New York congresswoman Geraldine Ferraro.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring and Assessment of the Golden Pioneer Museum and its Storage Facilities
ProjectDesc: For one year, monitor and record the environmental conditions of the Golden Pioneer Museum's exhibit and artifact storage areas. After that, for six months, compile the data, consult with conservators and other experts, and create a long-term conservation plan for the museum.
ToSupport: A storage environment consultation and the purchase and installation of monitoring equipment and supplies to assess temperature and relative humidity, air pollutants, pests, and light levels in storage and exhibit areas for a collection that reflects the history of Golden, Colorado.
Participants: Michael Thompson [Project Director]; Cornelia Bogaard [Project Director]; Theresa Morgan [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Assessing 18th- and 19th-Century New Hampshire Maps and Atlases
ProjectDesc: The New Hampshire State Library seeks $5,000 to support a collection level conservation assessment of its New Hampshire and New England maps and atlases collections. The activities entail hiring a maps preservation consultant to assess conservation needs and purchasing archival quality housing supplies to protect 150 maps and 50 atlases from the 18th and 19th centuries. The project is a continuation of a general collection conservation assessment conducted in 2002 which identified the state library's collections of early printed and manuscript maps as a preservation priority.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of the state library's New Hampshire and New England map and atlas collection from the 18th and 19th centuries, and the purchase of storage furniture and preservation supplies.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment, Workshop, and Purchase of Preservation Materials
ProjectDesc: A consultant will conduct an on-site visit for a general preservation assessment of the local history collection of Canton Public Library, Canton, Connecticut, Her report will enable us to set priorities and establish a long-range plan for preservation. Following the survey and report, a half-day workshop will be held tailored to our specific needs. A flat file and preservation materials and supplies will be purchased.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment, a training workshop, and the purchase of supplies for archives, manuscripts, photographs, maps, and oral history collections related to the history of Canton, Connecticut, from the 17th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Consolidation and Relocation of the Historic Speedwell Archives
ProjectDesc: The project will prepare the archival collection for relocation by consolidating it to one room, with the exception of duplicate-image storage of important documents off-site. Morris County Park Commission will establish environmental controls to the building as part of its 2004 5-year plan. Archivally appropriate, lightweight storage shelving and archival document boxes need to be purchased to complete the storage consolidation. This storage format will be a consistent and accessible organizational plan. To prepare for the consolidation prior to relocation, an extensive inventory was performed in 2004. Currently, a finding aid is being implemented to organize the collection which measures approximately 58 linear feet.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and purchase of storage supplies for archival holdings related to the Vail family and their ownership of the Speedwell Iron Works from 1790 to 1913 .
Participants: Diana Angione [Project Director]; Lynn Laffey [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Purchase Storage Materials to Preserve Works of Art
ProjectDesc: A grant of $4970 would enable the Stephen Phillips Trust House to complete a re-housing project of the art collection. The final 250 (of a total of 663) pieces need to be removed from inadequate locations and conditions and placed in a setting that meets current preservation standards. The funds would be used to purchase two art storage bins and one shelving unit for our off-site storage facility as well as archival supplies. The purpose of the project is twofold: to ensure the preservation of the collection and to make it accessible for future programming, exhibits and research.
ToSupport: The purchase of materials to rehouse 250 works of art in the collection of the Stephen Phillips Trust House.

ProjectTitle: Purchase of Storage Furniture and Preservation Supplies
ProjectDesc: The Rosenbach Museum & Library is applying for an NEH Preservation Assistance Grant that will fund the purchase of supplies for rehousing the museum's collection of maps and broadsides. The Rosenbach also seeks to purchase additional shelves and drawers for its existing storage units to accommodate an increased number of objects in this collection as well as its growing collection of work by Maurice Sendak. And last, the museum seeks to purchase a combination of three storage cabinets that will supplement its object storage areas and provide ongoing, temporary protection and security for objects that move in and out of storage for projects such as exhibitions and programs.
ToSupport: The purchase of supplies for rehousing the museum's maps and broadsides and a collection of works by the writer and illustrator, Maurice Sendak, and the temporary storage of objects used for exhibitions and programs.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment for Storage Improvement
ProjectDesc: The Fitchburg Historical Society will contract with a preservation consultant to make recommendations for the future location and best types of storage for the Fitchburg Historical Society collections (estimated 200,000 items) which are currently in our 6000 sq.-ft. headquarters. Last year the Society purchased a 5-story historic building with 14,000 sq. ft. on Main Street. The consultant will make recommendations for the new storage areas and the museum galleries and research library which will display and house artifacts and archives. The report will guide the board, staff, committee and architect’s planning. The grant will also pay for environmentally safe containers for fragile archives which will be packed before being moved.
ToSupport: Consultation with a preservation professional to plan for improved storage of artifacts, art, and archival materials that document the history of Fitchburg (known as "Machine City") from its settlement in 1735 to the present and that reflect the city's industrial history.
Participants: Betsy Hannula [Project Director]; Susan Roetzer [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment of Local History Collections
ProjectDesc: With the proposed Preservation Assistance Grant, the Decatur Public Library will contract with The Conservation Center for Art and Historic Artifacts for conservator Mary Schobert to conduct a general preservation assessment of the library’s local history collections. The assessment will focus on two main objectives: 1) Assessing the conservation treatment needs of selected items in the local history collections; and 2) Developing recommendations for physical building improvements, climate controls, lighting, floor plan, and equipment for relocating the local history room from its current 2,000 square foot space into a 19,700 square foot local history/museum space (currently unfinished space within the Decatur Public Library building).
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of local, genealogical, book, and photographic collections related to the history of Decatur, Illinois, from the 19th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment and Training Workshop
ProjectDesc: This NEH Preservation Assistance grant would provide funds to hire a consultant. The consultant will conduct a preservation site assessment of library collections, with an emphasis on special collections, make recommendations for action, and provide a workshop. Volunteers and employees from local cultural heritage institutions will be invited to attend the workshop. The results of this grant will be to empower library staff to make needed improvements to the storage of library materials and historical documents. Local cultural heritage institutions will also benefit from the opportunity to learn more about the care of their collections.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the special collections of the University of Arkansas-Monticello Library and a preservation training workshop for staff of the library and of other cultural heritage institutions in the area.

ProjectTitle: Museum Security Assessment
ProjectDesc: The Detroit Historical Museums and Society (DHMS) is proposing a project that would include a comprehensive security assessment for each of the three sites that house our collections: the Main Museum, the Dossin Great Lakes Museum, and Historic Fort Wayne. A comprehensive written report after the survey is complete will include detailed recommendations and suggestions to bring the institution into full compliance with the “Suggested Guidelines for Museum Security.” The goal of this project is for the DHMS to have a comprehensive and integrated security plan for each of the sites in order to maintain the integrity of our collections.
ToSupport: An assessment of the security needs at the Detroit Historical Museum, the Dossin Great Lakes Museum, and Historic Fort Wayne, which house 150,000 artifacts reflecting the history of Detroit and southeastern Michigan.

ProjectTitle: Purchase of Storage Furniture to Rehouse Military Miniatures Collection
ProjectDesc: The Preservation Assistance Grant would support the preservation of Heritage Museums & Gardens’ 6,000 piece collection of military miniatures through the purchase of archival storage furniture. This collection is the first in the museum to undergo a thorough process of inventory, condition assessment and photography, rehousing and records digitization. Through the purchase of four archival-quality cabinets, the museum will not only be able to mitigate detrimental environmental conditions, but, by providing designated and systematic storage for the largest collection in its holdings, will be able to maintain more accurate and secure locations and therefore improved accountability for the objects in years in come.
ToSupport: The purchase of cabinets for the storage of a collection of military miniatures comprised of approximately 6,000 figures organized into regiments that served from the colonial period to 1900.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Archives
ProjectDesc: The Perkins Archives are a rich resource in the history of the education of people who are blind or deafblind, for the life of Helen Keller, and for local history. However, the materials have never been organized or catalogued, and finding information is extremely difficult or even impossible. The Perkins Research Library is applying for an NEH Preservation Assistance Grant to hire a qualified preservationist/archivist to evaluate the preservation and organization needs of the Archives. Perkins will use the archivist’s written assessment as a guideline for its long-range plans to arrange, describe, preserve, and catalog the material in its Archives.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of correspondence, manuscripts, photographs, and books related to the history of a noted school for the blind, 1820s to the present.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Oversized Teaching Collections at Rare Book School
ProjectDesc: This project will support the purchase of furniture and preservation supplies necessary to rehouse Rare Book School's oversized teaching collections. Affected collections include 702 prints and 1,730 specimens of papermaking, bibliographical format, typography, and manuscript. With the purchase of six five-drawer flat file units, RBS will redistribute this collection, relocate oversized materials currently in remote storage to files where they are immediately needed in class, and plan for future growth of oversized collections. In addition, RBS will purchase polyester, foil-backed labels, and acid-free boxes to improve existing storage within its collections of oversized prints and specimens.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture and preservation supplies to house oversized teaching materials, including 700 prints and 1,730 specimens of papermaking, typography, illustration processes, and manuscript leaves.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment
ProjectDesc: The South Kingstown Public Library will contract with the Northeast Document Conservation Center to conduct a General Preservation Planning Survey. The purpose of the survey is to identify hazards to collections overall and to help preserve materials using preventive maintenance strategies. Building conditions, storage and handling procedures, disaster preparedness and policies that impact preservation will be examined. The consultant will prepare a formal report which will be used as a first step in the Library's long-term preservation initiative.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of archives, photographs, newspapers, and books related to Rhode Island state history.

ProjectTitle: A Preservation Assessment of the Women's Studio Workshop Archive
ProjectDesc: WSW is requesting $2,720 from NEH to work with preservation professional Erica Blumenfeld to review WSW's archival materials and develop a detailed plan for rehousing the collection. Activities include reviewing current collections storage, discussing future plans for the materials & going over policies & practices for archive use. A written report will contain prioritized recommendations for future preservation action.
ToSupport: General preservation and archival management assessments in preparation for the rehousing of archival collections related to the history of a grassroots feminist arts studio and the printmakers, photographers, and other women artists in residence from 1974 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Purchase Storage Materials for the American Geographical Society Library Rare Atlas Collection
