ProjectDesc: This funding will support the re-housing of approximately 100 of the 2,200 rare atlases in the AGS Library (1478-1900). The emphasis of this project will be selected world atlases published from 1570 to 1830. This is a long-standing priority of the AGS Library and a key recommendation of the NEH funded preservation assessment (April 2004). The AGSL, begun with the Society, in 1851, was transferred to UW-Milwaukee in 1978. It is a vital resource for humanities research. Although considerable effort has recently gone into the preservation of its resources, the results of the absence of preservation funding prior to 1978 are painfully evident. The reversal of this deterioration has become a leading long-term goal of the library.
ToSupport: Purchase of hinged acid-free boxes to rehouse approximately 100 rare world atlases, published between 1570 and 1830, in the collection of the American Geographical Society Library of the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee.

ProjectTitle: Disaster Response Training and Environmental Monitoring at the University of Montana-Missoula
ProjectDesc: Grant support would fund three activities. First, grant funding would bring a trained professional to the Maureen and Mike Mansfield Library at The University of Montana-Missoula to teach a full-day hands-on Disaster Recovery workshop for the Mansfield Library’s newly established Disaster Response Team. Second, grant support would pay for a full-day disaster planning workshop to be offered to Mansfield Library affiliates and librarians, archivists and curators from the region. Third, grant funding would allow the Mansfield Library to purchase 3 IPI Preservation Environment Monitors (PEM) for continuous monitoring of temperature and humidity throughout the library building.
ToSupport: Training in disaster recovery for the staff of the Maureen and Mike Mansfield Library of the University of Montana-Missoula and for other librarians and archivists in the region. The grant would also allow the purchase of environmental monitoring equipment for the Mansfield Library.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of the Television News Film and Video Archive
ProjectDesc: The Historical Society of Central Florida has among its collections a large archive of television broadcast film. This proposal supports the hiring of a professional conservator with the appropriate qualifications to provide the Historical Society with an assessment of the conservation needs of the collection. In addition the Historical Society will request advice from the conservator on storage and preservation of the current film collection (including a list of required supplies and equipment purchases), recommendations for the appropriate migration of the collection to a more stable and user friendly media such as digital media, and recommendations for creating a cataloguing system for the newly migrated collection.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of a collection of 2 million feet of local television news coverage donated to the society by WDBO-TV that dates from 1954 through the 1970s that documents the recent history of central Florida.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Works On Paper at the L.C.Bates Museum
ProjectDesc: The L.C.Bates Museum proposes to hire paper conservator, Walter Newman, Director of Paper Conservation at Northeast Document Conservation Center to conduct an on-site collection level conservation assessment of paper-based materials including photographs, documents, manuscripts, ephemera, architectural plans, and works of art. One project goal is to implement the recommendations of our 1992 CAP and 2000 CPS object survey that recommend that we have expert professional detailed assessments to plan care and treatment for specific Museum collections.
ToSupport: A consultant's preservation assessment of paper-based materials, such as photographs, documents, manuscripts, architectural plans and works of art, in the collections of the L.C. Bates Museum.

Institution: Historical Society of Seattle and King County
ProjectTitle: Purchase of Environmental Monitoring Equipment and Training
ProjectDesc: The Museum of History & Industry (MOHAI) is taking steps to strengthen the preservation of its collections of more than 2 million historic artifacts, photographs and archival materials. MOHAI will purchase state-of-the-art environmental monitoring equipment, software and accessories for use in the museum galleries, collections storage areas and MOHAI’s Sophie Frye Bass Research Library. MOHAI will purchase four Preservation Environment Monitors (PEMs) by Image Permanence Institute of Rochester, NY. MOHAI will also purchase the associated software, "Climate Notebook," which aids in analyzing data. MOHAI will also train its collections and library staff on how to use PEMs and Climate Notebook software.
ToSupport: The purchase of equipment and the training of staff to monitor environmental conditions in exhibition and storage spaces for a collection of more than two million historic artifacts, photographs, and archival materials that document domestic life, culture, business, and industry in the Pacific Northwest from early Euro-American settlement to the present.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of the Archives in Brennan Library at Lasell College
ProjectDesc: Winslow Archives seeks funding to hire a consultant for a preservation survey. The survey will provide an assessment of the Archives’ environment, security and collections. The consultant will assess the new room built in 2005 and the existing room that houses the Archives for issues of environment, security and space use. The consultant will also assess the Archives collections which include: College publications, and records,course catalogs,yearbooks,student publications, a large photograph collection,personal student ephemera, scrapbooks, letters and newspaper clippings,etc. The consultant’s survey report will provide the guidance for the collections’ storage and handling and long range planning for the Archives.
ToSupport: An assessment of the preservation, security, facility, and management needs of a collection of correspondence, ledger books, scrapbooks, photographs, yearbooks, and ephemera related to the history of the college, founded in 1851.

ProjectTitle: Purchase of Storage Furniture and Light Control Material
ProjectDesc: A Preservation Assistance Grant is requested to purchase record storage racks to safely house approximately 2,000 archival records, manuscripts, documents, photographs, and artifacts and a steel filing cabinet to house collection records in safe, secure storage. UV filtering plastic will be installed to windows in the exhibition gallery, library, and collection storage to protect collection materials from damaging ultra-violet light. The plan of work will significantly improve the care, use, and preservation of the Erie Canal Museum's unique Erie Canal-related collection materials and addresses storage and light control issues identified in the Museum's 2003 IMLS CAP survey.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage racks and a cabinet for archival holdings that document the construction and maintenance of the Erie Canal in New York state. Ultraviolet filtering film would be purchased to protect the museum's exhibition and research areas from light.

ProjectTitle: Institute of American Indian Arts Archives Preservation Project
ProjectDesc: The Institute of American Indian Arts (IAIA) requests $5000 from the NEH Preservations Assistance Grants for Smaller Institutions. These funds would allow IAIA to hire a professional archivist to conduct a general preservation assessment of the Institute’s archives and to help draft a long-range plan for the care of this historical collection. These funds would additionally support the purchase of preservation supplies such as storage containers, and the reorganization of the archive's paper objects, slides and videotapes into this new storage. Funding for these activities would improve the ability for IAIA to preserve and care for its historical archives.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and the purchase of rehousing supplies for an archives that documents American Indian arts.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment and Plan
ProjectDesc: Pewabic Pottery is seeking funding to support a general preservation assessment of our paper humanities collections. The Pottery would like to hire a paper conservator from Rivers Paper Conservation and Preservation Services to assess the needs of our collection and make recommendations for treatment priorities as well as for housing and storage. The overall goal of this project is improve the Pottery’s ability to preserve and care for our historical documents for generations to come.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of Pewabic Pottery's archival collection of historic photographs, drawings, blueprints, and other documents relating to the work of the Stratton studio.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring Project
ProjectDesc: The funds for this project will be used to purchase environmental monitoring equipment of humanities collections: nine dataloggers to monitor the temperature and humidity in the research collections housed in the Klamath County Museums' main building. This request is based upon findings of the museum consultant (Tamsen Fuller)who did a Conservation Survey and Assessment report in 2001 (CAP). She recommeded that we monitor and record temperature and humidity for a year through the building, so that we can make the best decisions about actions to preserve Klamath County's history.
ToSupport: The purchase of environmental monitoring equipment to measure relative humidity and temperature in the county's main museum, which houses court, election, and land records, tax rolls, photographs, and other materials related to the history of Klamath County from the 1880s to 1976.

ProjectTitle: Preserving the History of Marian College and its Campus
ProjectDesc: The Preservation Assistance Grant will support the purchase of supplies, storage furniture and environmental monitoring and lighting equipment for the Marian College Archives in the Mother Theresa Hackelmeier Memorial Library, as recommended in a preservation assessment report prepared in 2004. The Archives house documents, photos, blueprints and other materials related to the history of Marian College from 1937 to the present, as well as information about the lives and former estates of James, Allison, Carl Fisher and Frank Wheeler, three of the founders of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway and the Indianapolis 500 race whose estates comprise the Marian campus.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture, environmental monitoring equipment, and preservation supplies to rehouse textual records related to college history as well as manuscripts and other materials of the founders of the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, whose former estates now comprise the Marian College campus.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Plan for Archives at Packwood House Museum
ProjectDesc: The Packwood House Museum is requesting funds to hire Valerie Metzler, archivist and historian, to conduct a preservation needs assessment of the archival collections. She will assess the current condition of the Museum’s archival collections, develop a plan for arrangement and description, and determine what materials are needed to properly rehouse them. The outcome of the project would be a report that describes the next steps for arrangement, description, and cataloging, as well as a detailed listing of the supplies that would be needed to properly store the entire collection in a way that not only preserves it, but makes it more useful to a broad public.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment and the development of an archival management plan to preserve the personal papers of the museum's founders and manuscripts, correspondence, books, and other materials related to the institution.

ProjectTitle: Establishing a Long-Term Environmental Monitoring Program
ProjectDesc: Historic Hope Foundation, Inc., (HHF) is requesting a Preservation Assistance Grant of $4,939 to establish an environmental monitoring program for the historic buildings housing the museum’s collections. Through this project HHF will (1) purchase dataloggers for collections areas, a data transporter, data management software, and a lux meter; (2) install the loggers and establish a monitoring program and environmental control targets in consultation with preventive conservator Catherine Anderson of Colonial Williamsburg Foundation; (3) analyze 9 months of data; (4) prioritize environmental needs for the collections areas and plan for more comprehensive treatments based on Ms. Anderson’s recommendations.
ToSupport: The purchase and installation of equipment to monitor environmental conditions in Historic Hope Plantation's two historic buildings, which display collections of North Carolina furniture, textiles, decorative arts, and household artifacts.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Needs Assessment for the Special Collections and Archives
ProjectDesc: The W. Frank Steely Library at Northern Kentucky University proposes to develop a long-range plan for the care of its special collections in the Department of Special Collections and Archives. With funding from the Preservation Assistance Grant we will utilize the expertise of a consultant to conduct a preservation needs assessment. The consultant will assess the general condition of the collections, and its organization, housing, security, and storage environment and submit a final report summarizing prioritized recommendations for our collections' long-term care and needs. The consultant will also recommend supplies to be purchased that will support the preservation of the collections.
ToSupport: A preservation needs assessment of the environment of the Department of Special Collections and Archives and the condition of its collections, which document the history of northern Kentucky and the greater Cincinnati region during the last two hundred years. The consultant would advise on the long-term care of the collections and recommend supplies for purchase.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing the Photograph Collection of the Andover Historical Society
ProjectDesc: With the proposed Preservation Assistance Grant, the Andover Historical Society will re-house and relocate a portion of its photograph collection. The photograph collection is currently stored in acid-free folders in hanging files and vertical filing cabinets in the Historical Society’s library. If awarded, the Preservation Assistance Grant will purchase appropriately-sized photographic print sleeves and flat and clamshell archival storage boxes to re-house 2,000 of the 15,400 photographs and stereopticon views in the photograph collection.
ToSupport: The purchase of archival supplies to rehouse a collection of 2,000 photographs and stereopticon views dating from 1840 to the present that document the history and culture of Andover, Massachusetts.
Participants: Barbara Brown [Project Director]; Elena Sarni [Project Director]

Institution: Town of Warrensburg Museum of Local History
ProjectTitle: Condition Assessment, Storage Needs, and Training Workshop
ProjectDesc: The Warrensburg Museum of Local History contains a collection of more than 300 articles of apparel and other textiles, dating from the early nineteenth century into the mid twentieth century. To reverse years of neglect the Town seeks a professional assessment of the collection’s condition, to learn proper cleaning techniques and correct storage procedures, and to obtain appropriate storage materials. The Town has enlisted the support of members of the Warrensburgh Historical Society to perform these procedures, once properly trained. This collection was donated by local townspeople in the 1970s and 1980s after the Museum’s founding in 1975.
ToSupport: Hiring a preservation specialist to conduct an assessment of the textile collection of the Warrensburg Museum of Local History and to lead a workshop for staff and volunteers on cleaning textiles and proper storage procedures. The museum will also purchase storage materials to rehouse the collection.

Institution: Penobscot Marine Museum Maine's Oldest Maritime Museum
ProjectTitle: Conservation of Collections at Penobscot Marine Museum
ProjectDesc: Funding will support a one-day conservation assessment targeting specific issues of light levels and rotation of artifacts in historic house exhibit buildings. We are also asking for thermohygrometers for our exhibit and storage areas. Anticipated purchases are shades, thermohygrometers, Blue Wool standard cards, and storage tubes.
ToSupport: Hiring a conservation consultant to conduct an assessment of the exposure of textiles to light levels in 2 historic house museums and the purchase of materials.

ProjectTitle: Mattress Factory Archives Preservation
ProjectDesc: The Mattress Factory museum of contemporary art requests $5,000 from the NEH Preservation Assistance Grant program to support purchase of archival storage materials and furniture, especially for electronic and digital media-related materials. For close to 30 years, the Mattress Factory has supported the creation and presentation of new installation art by more than 250 artists, many of whom were leaders in the field of contemporary art. Archival collections amassed during this time are being organized and inventoried by a part-time Archivist. She will use the materials purchased through this grant to rehouse archival items in appropriate storage containers.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture and archival supplies to rehouse a multimedia collection that documents the organization's contemporary art collection and the lives of 250 artists and their works.

Institution: Eastern Shore of Virginia Historical Society
ProjectTitle: Preserving Archival Collections
ProjectDesc: The Eastern Shore of Virginia Historical Society seeks an NEH Preservation Assistance Grant for Smaller Institutions to purchase storage furniture and preservation supplies for the Archive and Library located in Ker Place (ca. 1800), the Society's headquarters and historic house museum. The grant funds will be used to complete the proper storage for the Society's archival collections of bibles, ledgers, scrapbooks, three manuscript collections and the Dr. John Robertson photograph and Bell glass slide negatives collections.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture and preservation supplies for birth, death, marriage and other vital records, manuscripts, personal correspondence, ledgers, photographs, and records related to the history of Virginia's Eastern Shore from the 17th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Conservation Assessment of the Barnard College Archives
ProjectDesc: The project will use a professional document conservator to visit the Barnard College Archives to conduct a treatment assessment of 18 archival scrapbooks. Total collection is 27; the other 9 were previously examined in 2004. Contents include photographs, handwritten letters, clippings, and ephemera documenting the academic and social culture at Barnard from 1901-1947; intercollegiate activities; social movements such as women's suffrage; and women's service during WWI and WWII. The conservator will spend up to 2.5 days on site, measuring, analyzing, and evaluating the scrapbooks. S/he will spend 1 day writing a conservation assessment report that will support future grant proposals for the conservation and microfilming of the scrapbooks.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of eighteen scrapbooks containing photographs, letters, clippings, and ephemera that document the activities of an independent liberal arts college for women from 1901 to 1947.

ProjectTitle: Assessment to Preserve the Historical Records of Exempla Saint Joseph Hospital
ProjectDesc: This project will assess the need for strengthening and preserving the historical and cultural archival materials of Exempla Saint Joseph Hospital. It will also initiate development of policies for accessioning materials and for making the collection more accessible to researchers. Exempla Saint Joseph Hospital was founded in 1873 as the first private hospital in Denver, Colorado. The Hospital has had a significant role in the history of Denver. The proposed assessment will be the first step in assuring the future preservation of a unique set of records.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of records related to the institutional history of a private hospital established in Denver by the Sisters of Charity in 1873.

ProjectTitle: Conservation Plan for the Museum of Anthropology's Collections
ProjectDesc: The Museum of Anthropology will hire a conservator to work with staff in producing a long-range conservation plan for 27,433 archaeological and ethnographic objects. The conservator will visit the Museum to assess policies, practices, and conditions that affect the care and preservation of collections and will prepare a report that summarizes his findings and prioritizes recommendations for future preservation actions. The document will be a key element in developing a collections plan to focus collecting activities and guide controlled future growth and deaccessioning. It will guide development of a disaster plan and the design process for a storage facility to hold the collections, currently in crowded and unstable conditions.
ToSupport: Consultation with a conservator to produce a long-range plan for the preservation of 27,433 archaeological and ethnographic artifacts in the university's Museum of Anthropology.

ProjectTitle: Environmental Monitoring Project
ProjectDesc: Based upon recommendations in the general conservation assessment survey prepared by Neil Cockerline of the Upper Midwest Conservation Association, the Olmsted County Historical Society plans to purchase and install thirty HOBO Data Loggers throughout the History Center, Mayowood Mansion, Dee Log Cabin, Hadley Valley Schoolhouse, and Stoppel Barn. The methodology also includes developing procedures and standards for monitoring buildings and collections, investigating solutions for troubled areas, submitting data logger information to staff and the Board of Directors, and incorporating environment improvement projects into the long-range strategic plan and preservation plan.
ToSupport: The purchase and installation of equipment to monitor environmental conditions in the society's history center and its four historic buildings, which store and display some 20,000 artifacts and the extensive archival holdings focused on the history of Olmsted County, Minnesota, from the 1850s to the present. Included are materials related to the history of such local enterprises as the Mayo Clinic and IBM Rochester.

ProjectTitle: Training for Care and Preservation of Photograph Collections
ProjectDesc: The New Castle Historical Society requests funds to send its curator/collections manager Rebecca Wilson to the week-long program "Preserving Photographs in a Digital World" in August 2006. The program sponosored by the George Eastman House, the Image Permanence Institute, and the Rochester Institute of Technology covers photographic preservation technology, archival practices, and digital imaging. Wilson is in charge of all aspects of the Society's diverse collections. Attending the program would provide her with the information she needs to plan and administer short and long-term preservation plans for the Society's photograph collection.
ToSupport: Attendance by the society's curator/collections manager at a week-long workshop on photographic preservation in Rochester, New York, in August 2006.

ProjectTitle: Collection Storage Plan for Pennsbury Manor's New Visitor Center
ProjectDesc: This project will engage a consultant, Kory Berrett, to develop a plan for collection storage in Pennsbury Manor’s new Visitor Center storage area. The plan will include recommendations for specific storage furnishings and plans for their layout in the new storage area; it will allow Pennsbury to maximize space use within the available budget. The new storage area will ameliorate the currently inadequate storage conditions and expand available space to enable future additions to the collections.
ToSupport: A consultant's assessment of the collections storage area of the Pennsbury Society and development of an improved plan for safe storage of collections.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment at the University of Richmond Library
ProjectDesc: A Preservation Assistance Grant will allow Boatwright Memorial Library, University of Richmond to conduct a critical assessment of preservation needs for its humanities collections. Patricia Selinger, a consultant with expertise in library materials preservation, will be hired to assess current preservation activities, review the library’s disaster response procedures, and make recommendations for future staff training, equipment needs, building environmental systems, and priorities for implementing recommendations. In summer 2006, the library will renovate the two floors housing most of the humanities collections, and will incorporate the consultant’s preservation recommendations into this renovation plan and longer term strategies.
ToSupport: A preservation consultant's assessment of preservation activities, disaster response procedures, staff training, and preservation equipment for the care of humanities collections in Boatwright Library of the University of Richmond.

ProjectTitle: Purchase of Archival Storage Materials
ProjectDesc: The Howard Baker Center for Public Policy at the University of Tennessee requests $4,987 to purchase archival storage containers and archival folders for the collections of Senator Howard Baker, Jr.; Congressman John Duncan, Sr.; Congressman Howard Baker, Sr.; Congresswoman Irene Baker; and Governor Donald Sundquist. These collections are part of the Modern Political Archives, an intellectual entity consisting of the papers and archival material held by the University of Tennessee Libraries and the Baker Center relating to political leaders of Tennessee, major associates of those leaders, and other individuals or groups who have had a major impact on Tennessee during the modern era (1945 to present).
ToSupport: Purchase of boxes and folders to rehouse selected manuscripts in the Modern Political Archives collection of the university's Howard Baker Center for Public Policy.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assistance for Archives Storage and Supplies
ProjectDesc: The Dakota State University Historical Archives, located in the Karl E. Mundt Library, houses material dating from 1881 to the present. The collections relate to the history of Dakota State University, local history, and the history of public higher education in South Dakota. Shelving is needed to replace non-conservation shelving and to expand the shelving area to accommodate more material. Acid-free storage containers are needed to properly store and conserve collections. This project is based on the preservation assessment and recommendations of Neil C. Cockerline, Director of Field Services and Conservator of the Upper Midwest Conservation Association.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage shelving and preservation supplies to rehouse collections related to local history and to the institutional history of the university, 1881 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Purchase of Monitoring Equipment to Preserve Texas Hill Country Collections
ProjectDesc: Logan Library seeks materials and staff training to help us continue implementation of the first segment of a three-stage strategic plan for the long-term care of our collection. Our planning process began in 2002 with the help of an NEH Preservation Assistance Grant. While our efforts will attend the needs of our entire collection, we hope to also target specifically our Texas Hill Country Special Collection. We wish to follow the suggestions of consultant Jean Baldwin: purchase the required equipment, establish baseline procedures and policies for collection preservation, and implement a strategic plan for site improvement and staff training.
ToSupport: The purchase of environmental monitoring equipment, ultraviolet filtering sleeves, and appropriate storage equipment for the university's Texas Hill Country Collection and preservation training for members of the staff.

ProjectTitle: Frenchtown Heritage Museum Photographic Collection Housing and Storage
ProjectDesc: Award of a Preservation Assistance Grant for $5000 would enable the Frenchtown Heritage Museum (FHM) to purchase several units of open metal shelving that meet archival requirement, acid-free boxes and enclosures for the photographic types present in the collection as well as hire a consultant to begin rehousing and storage of the Museum's photo collection. The consultant would train the staff and volunteers to appropriately house and store the collection. During the grant period the consultant will also train how to evaluate originals, copy print and reproductions which are currently on display in teh Museum.
ToSupport: Consultation with a preservation specialist and the purchase of storage equipment and archival supplies to rehouse 3,000 still images in a variety of formats that document the history and culture of St. Charles city and county from the mid 19th century to the present.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Collections at Massanutten Regional Library.
ProjectDesc: The Massanutten Regional Library System proposes to hire a consultant to conduct a preservation needs assessment of its Genealogy and Local History collections. The consultant will conduct an on-site survey at two of the branches in the library system. Through visits and interviews, she will assess the condition, security, and environmental conditions of these collections. Her final report will make recommendations for improving security, improving environmental housing conditions, preserving and managing, reviewing the disaster plan, and defining on-going financial needs of the collection. In her letter of commitment the consultant recommends the purchase of environmental monitoring equipment in addition to the needs assessment.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment, the purchase of environmental monitoring equipment, and preservation materials for books, photographs, correspondence, audiotapes, and other records related to the history of Harrisonburg, Virginia, and the surrounding communities during the 19th and 20th centuries.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Iowa's Battle Flags from the Spanish-American War
ProjectDesc: The State Historical Society of Iowa requests a Preservation Assistance Grant of $5000 toward obtaining a specialty cabinet to house the Spanish-American flags within Iowa’s battle flag collection. The State Historical Society of Iowa is engaged in a multi-year project to stabilize and treat a collection of battle flags carried and captured by Iowa volunteer regiments. The requested cabinet is the 9th cabinet of the 12 required to complete this project. The cabinets are designed to the specifications of Fonda Thomsen of Textile Preservation Associates of Keedysville, MD. Delta Designs LTD of Topeka, Kansas, builds the cabinets to exact conservation specifications and the highest museum standards.
ToSupport: Purchasing storage furniture to rehouse the society's collection of battle flags. The flags belonged to Iowa volunteer regiments that fought in the Spanish-American War.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment of Lutheran Church Archives
ProjectDesc: A consultant from the Upper Midwest Conservation Association would be retained to conduct a general collections needs assessment survey for the Lutheran Church Archives, which is located in Folke Bernadotte Memorial Library. The survey report would address immediate conservation and preservation issues and provide guidelines for a long-term plan for the ongoing preservation of collections as a whole within the library setting. The survey would address all factors that directly affect the preservation of the archives collections and make recommendations as to how artifacts and rare books might be used for research, teaching, and exhibits without causing harm to fragile items.
ToSupport: A general preservation survey of library special collections that document the history and culture of Swedish Lutherans in the American Midwest since the 19th century.

ProjectTitle: Archival and Manuscript Collection Preservation Project
ProjectDesc: The Historical Society of Frankford (HSF) requests $5,000 for a project to preserve significant parts of its collection of seventeenth- through twentieth-century archives and manuscripts. The funds will be used to: 1) purchase archival storage supplies and equipment to re-house parts of the collection, 2) purchase equipment to monitor environmental conditions in HSF's archives space, and 3) pay for a training session on basic archival preservation practices for those who will be working with the collection. HSF is requesting the funds to implement recommendations in the recent report of its archival consultant, Jack McCarthy, who will serve as Project Director.
ToSupport: The purchase of environmental monitoring equipment, storage furniture, archival supplies, and a training workshop for archival, manuscript, and book collections related to the history of Philadelphia and the surrounding area from the 17th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of the Works on Paper Collection of Pomona College Museum of Art
ProjectDesc: Pomona College Museum of Art, with a consulting conservator, will assess the preservation needs of a 4000 object works on paper collection. The collection—prints, photographs, and drawings, including preparatory drawings for murals at Pomona College by José Clemente Orozco and Rico Lebrun—is one of three collection groups held by the Museum. The survey will yield recommendations for: 1. Short-term remediation of problems in housing, storage, including environmental factors, and increased collection access. 2. Long-range plans for collection storage in a new or significantly renovated museum facility. 3. Identification of objects for conservation assessment and treatment as part of an on-going collection care plan.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of 4000 works on paper, including prints, photographs, and drawings from the 16th to the 19th century, and the training of a staff member in collections care.

ProjectTitle: Contemporary Chinese Photography Conservation
ProjectDesc: In December 2004, the David and Alfred Smart Museum of Art, University of Chicago (“the Smart”) acquired a substantial body of large-scale contemporary Chinese photographs, adding significantly to its already impressive collection of experimental photography-based work from contemporary China. This addition to the Smart’s permanent collection follows its recent world-traveling exhibition "Between Past and Future: New Photography from China," whose tour encompasses New York, Chicago, Seattle, London, Santa Barbara, and Berlin. A Preservation Assistance Grant would support two key activities: a general preservation assessment of the photography in the museum’s collection and staff training in photographic preservation.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of a collection of 41 contemporary Chinese photographs acquired by the university's David and Alfred Smart Museum of Art, a visual arts repository. A small portion of the grant would subsidize attendance by the society's registrar at a week-long workshop on photographic preservation in Rochester, New York, in August 2006.

ProjectTitle: Improving Lighting and Storage
ProjectDesc: The purpose of this project is to address some of the chief preservation concerns of the collections conservator, Jodie Utter of East West Paper Conservation in Memphis, TN, as expressed in a 2004 IMLS/CAP report. Ms. Utter found the reduction of light levels in the exhibit rooms as well as in the archive and storage spaces an area for immediate attention. She also focused on improving storage and methods of storage as another area for immediate attention. Our goal is to install shades on the windows and UV film on fluorescent bulbs in the exhibit areas and acquire shelving and other storage materials in order to preserve the artifacts in our care and to make them more readily accessible.
ToSupport: The implementation of light control measures and the purchase of storage shelving to preserve a 10,000-item artifact and archival collection that documents the history of Nevada County, Arkansas, from its settlement, through the Civil War and the coming of the railroad, and into the 20th century.

Institution: General Lew Wallace Study and Museum
ProjectTitle: Preservation Storage Improvements
ProjectDesc: The General Lew Wallace Study & Museum (GLWSM) requests a Preservation Assistance Grant of $5,000 to improve the storage shelving and housing of its collections. Currently, the collection is housed in off-site storage with minimal climate control and no archival storage shelving or housing materials. This grant award will provide sufficient housing for the collection in the new Carriage House Interpretive Center, scheduled to open in late 2005. The Center’s plans include a restricted, climate controlled collections storage room that will accommodate the existing collection and future accessions. The grant award will provide a portion of the total project budget of $16,421.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage supplies and furniture to rehouse collections that document the life of General Lew Wallace (1827-1905), the author of "Ben-Hur," a major general in the Union army, governor of the New Mexico Territory, and minister to Turkey. The collections include published literary works and memorabilia from motion pictures and stage productions of "Ben-Hur," in addition to historical objects, archival materials, photographs, paintings, and sketches with documented provenance to General Wallace and his family.

Institution: Customs House Museum and Cultural Center
ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment
ProjectDesc: We are applying to NEH to fund the services of textile conservation specialist, A. Newbold Richardson, for preliminary activities supporting the museum’s textile re-housing project. Her consultant services in this project for us will include: A textile handling, care, and storage workshop for our staff and volunteers, A storage and handling survey of the 1,800 textiles involved in the re-housing,Direction in the choice of new textile storage units, and The layout design for the new textile storage area and object maintenance workspace. Support from this grant will also fund the purchase of a new archival vacuum for the maintenance of the textile objects. This is the first stage of the larger textile re-housing project.
ToSupport: Hiring a conservation specialist to conduct an assessment of the museum's textile collection. The consultant would also conduct a workshop for the museum's volunteers and staff on the handling, care, and storage of textiles. The consultant's report would provide recommendations for appropriate shelving as well as the design of the storage area.
Participants: Steven Stewart [Project Director]; Ned Crouch [Project Director]; Amy Andersen-Rude [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Prints and Drawings Collections at the Lewis Walpole Library
ProjectDesc: For this project, the Library will hire a professional conservation consultant who specializes in works of art on paper to conduct a general preservation assessment of the prints and drawings collections. The Conservator will then work with the Curator to develop a comprehensive plan for conservation treatments as necessary. The resulting improvements in the preservation of these humanities collections will insure that they continue to be available as an important resource in the United States for the study of eighteenth-century Anglo-American culture and aesthetics.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of the 18th-century British prints and drawings in the Lewis Walpole Library, and the development of a comprehensive plan for conservation treatment as needed for the 30,000 items in the collection.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of the New Hampshire Aviation Historical Society's Humanities Collection
ProjectDesc: The proposed Preservation Assistance Grant, will enable the New Hampshire Aviation Historical Society [NHAHS] to engage the services of Betsy Hamlin-Morin, a professional Archivist, to conduct an initial preservation assessment of the archival collection. This assessment will be conducted in three phases: To Identify and prioritize preservation needs of NHAHS archive/museum facility and collections using the guidelines of the New England Document Conservation Center [NEDCC] self survey. To recommend professionally accepted best preservation practices through which original materials will be safeguarded for use in educational programs, research and exhibits. To establish a long-range schedule and budget for ongoing preservation.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of artifacts, art, and archives related to the history of aviation in New Hampshire.

ProjectTitle: Collections Preservation Project
ProjectDesc: Upholding its commitment to the preservation and care of collections, the Sonoma County Museum is requesting support for a collections preservation assessment of the Museum's collection, with an emphasis on three-dimensional objects. The Museum will hire an independent collections management and conservation consultant to conduct a general preservation assessment including evaluation of current policies, practices, and conditions affecting the care and preservation of collections. Additionally the consultant will develop a plan for improving collections storage and recommend future action. The consultant will also conduct a workshop on preservation and storage issues for Museum staff. Nearby organizations will be invited to participate.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of the museum's collections of fine and decorative art, textiles and clothing, furniture and household objects, tools, and equipment, which document the history and culture of Sonoma County.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Local History Archives
ProjectDesc: With funding from the NEH Preservation Assistance Grant, the Historical Society of Rockland County will use the services of Conservator Nelly Balloffet of Paper Star Assoc., Inc. to provide a general preservation assessment of the Library archival collections comprised of 10,000+ pieces. This survey will focus on both immediate preservation recommendations and recommendations for a proposed move of the library to a larger space.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the artifact collection and the local history library related to the heritage of Rockland County, New York, since the late 18th century.

Institution: John Wesley Powell River History Museum
ProjectTitle: Archival Preservation Training and Storage Environment Monitoring Project
ProjectDesc: The John Wesley Powell River History Museum will use the grant funds to hire a conservator to implement a storage and environmental improvement project for the archives housed in the JWP Museum. The assistance of a professional conservator is required to: 1) aid in the development of a Long Range Conservation Plan, 2) train staff and volunteers in proper handling, cataloging, and storage of archives, 3) recommend storage furniture and supplies, and 4) implement proper housing techniques. Grant funds will also be used to upgrade the archives room and properly house the current collection of maps, photographs, diaries, journals, and newspapers.
ToSupport: Training and the purchase of supplies and an environmental monitor to improve the storage and handling of the museum's archives and photographs depicting the history of settlement in Green River, Utah, since the 1870s.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Library Special Collections
ProjectDesc: The Library of The Mint Museums will contract with conservator Carol Paulson Crawford to conduct a preservation assessment of the library’s special collections, totaling approximately 2,500 items. The assessment will identify the preservation needs of the collections, recommend the actions needed for the conservation of materials and provide a long-range plan for their preservation and accessible storage and the necessary allocation of resources. Ms. Crawford will conduct in-house training for the Librarian in conservation treatments and preservation activities. Also, the Librarian will attend SOLINET preservation workshops for training in preservation of library materials to increase staff knowledge of collection preservation requirements.
ToSupport: A preservation needs assessment of the library's special collections of rare books that support the Mint Museum's holdings of art, which include ceramics, pre-Columbian art, and graphic arts; and preservation training for the librarian.

Institution: North Star Museum of Boy Scouting and Girl Scouting
ProjectTitle: North Star Museum Collections Conservation Assessment
ProjectDesc: The Museum will hire a conservator to assess collection, its state of preservation and storage. She will report to the Museum her findings, along with recommendations for storage priorities, rehousing priorities, and treatments, if they are necessary. The remainder of the grant money will be used for two purposes: buying data loggers, a light meter, and an aspirated psychrometer in order to more closely monitor the environment in our new building (purchased 4/05, occupied 9/05); provide a one-day collections care workshop for up to 20 staff and volunteers of this museum and other neighboring ones.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of a 150,000-item collection comprising artifacts, textiles, books and magazines, archival records, photographs, films and audiotapes that document the history of the Boy Scouts and the Girl Scouts from 1910 to the present.

ProjectTitle: Staff Training and General Preservation Assessment of the Archive Collection
ProjectDesc: Archivist Polly Darnell will conduct an on-site general preservation assessment of the Society’s archival collection generating 1) recommendations for the improvement of storage facilities, materials, and equipment, 2) draft plan for improving the arrangement of archival materials and creating useful finding aids, and 3) evaluation of current practices and policies and recommendations on how to improve access to materials. Consultant will help RAS draft a long-range plan for the care of our humanities collections. A training workshop will be given, and five members of RAS will enroll in an online workshop on archives from AASLH.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment and training workshops to preserve manuscripts, correspondence, books, and other materials related to the local history of Rehoboth, Massachusetts, from the 17th through the 19th century.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment of Archival Collections
ProjectDesc: The Bristol Historical Society has moved from a small homestead setting to the former Bristol High School (circa 1890) which has over 35,000 sf of exhibition space. The BHS is conducting the restoration of the building and is now faced with a myriad of collection storage issues including physical lay-out and renovation of research and public display areas; as well as storage space to conform with best practices; the need to identify and purchase proper storage units and materials; and to identify and environmental or building risks associated with the Society's new location, as well as protecting the collection during the renovations.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of photographs, postcards, correspondence, and artworks, related primarily to the 19th-century history of Bristol, Connecticut.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment for Genealogy, Local History, and Image Collections.
ProjectDesc: This conservation assessment will focus on a subset of our Special Collections—namely, the Genealogy Collection, the Hampshire Room which deals with local history, and the Special Collections Room which houses the Image Collection. These collections comprise several thousand individual objects relevant to local history ranging from the handwritten Civil War diary of Seth Pomeroy, records from town offices, stereographic images of the Williamsburg Flood, tens of thousands of photographic images, and extensive genealogy resources of Hampshire County and the region. It is essential that we take this fist step to preserving these invaluable resources.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of local, genealogical, and photographic collections related to the Pioneer Valley region of Massachusetts from the 19th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Audiovisual Collections Preservation Assessment and Training
ProjectDesc: The National Civil Rights Museum will contract with Amigos Library Services to conduct a preservation assessment of the museum’s audio-visual collections, specifically our collection of moving images. The assessment will produce recommendations for the following: § Short-term actions to improve storage conditions including physical plant recommendations and management of limited storage space. § Equipment and software recommendations for optimal documentation and preservation of audio-visual collections § Long-term plan for refreshment of media types, long-term storage recommendations Three members of the museum’s collections management staff will attend two training sessions between January 2006 and June 2007.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of 1,100 items in the museum's moving image collection created during the past 60 years and documenting the Civil Rights era in the United States.
Participants: Tracy Lauritzen Wright [Project Director]; Barbara Andrews [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Conservation Assessment for Art Gallery and Carriage Museum
ProjectDesc: GCVM proposes to hire conservator Barbara Moore to conduct a general conservation assessment of its John L. Wehle Art Gallery and Carriage Museum. The conservator will review a 1998 environmental survey which briefly mentions the two facilities. She will then document the physical and environmental conditions under which the collections in each are exhibited and stored. This review will consider environmental factors, including lighting, dust, temperature, relative humidity, and pests; evaluate current physical storage methods, storage equipment and supplies; review exhibit methods; and provide guidance for improvement.
ToSupport: A consultant's preservation assessment of the art and artifact collections held by the Genesee Country Village and Museum.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Archival Collections
ProjectDesc: The Saugatuck Douglas Historical Society requests a grant in order to conduct a General Preservation Assessment. The Society's collection is in photographs and related paper items that mirror the area's importance in the invention of summertime leisure and arts-related culture in the American Great Lakes region.
ToSupport: A preservation and access assessment for an archives and manuscript collection that documents the development of the Great Lakes region from the mid 19th century to the present.

ProjectTitle: Centennial Decade Scrapbook Preservation Project
ProjectDesc: This project will enable the Museum to hire a professional book conservator from the NEDCC to assess its unique set of 66 historical scrapbooks that capture and chronicle the cultural history of the Museum, community and region (1909-1992), and are in a critical stage of deterioration. This grant will support a training workshop for the Museum staff, library volunteers, and colleagues from local organizations that will focus on preservation and conservation strategies for scrapbooks, including actions that can be taken in-house by non-conservators. In addition, the grant will cover costs to purchase and ship the archival supplies recommended by the conservator to properly preserve and house the scrapbooks for continued research.
ToSupport: A conservation assessment of scrapbooks that document the history of the museum and the surrounding community and region, from 1909 through 1992, and a scrapbook preservation workshop for staff, volunteers, and colleagues from neighboring institutions.

ProjectTitle: General Preservation Assessment of the Berkshire Theatre Festival Archive Collection
ProjectDesc: With support from the National Endowment for the Humanities, the Berkshire Theatre Festival(BTF) will hire a consultant from the Northeast Document Conservation Center. The consultant will conduct a general preservation survey of the BTF archives with the purpose of identifying priorities both short and long term for the preservation of the theatre's present archival material and future materials.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of the Berkshire Theatre Festival archives that documents regional theater in Massachusetts since 1928.

ProjectTitle: Purchase Monitoring Equipment for Storage and Work Area for Rural Life Museum Collections
ProjectDesc: In 2002 Mars Hill College hired Etherington Conservation Center to evaluate current status of Ramsey Center holdings, and prioritize steps for their long-term management. With current request, Mars Hill addresses most urgent recommendations: make improvements in existing 1370 sq. ft. storage space--3rd level of the old library stacks--to provide secure, climate-controlled storage and work area for assessing physical condition of museum objects and appraising relevance to Ramsey Center mission. Budget includes onsite consultant to oversee process and train staff and purchase of shelving and essential environmental monitoring and cleaning equipment.
ToSupport: The purchase of environmental monitoring and cleaning equipment, preservation supplies and materials, and training of staff in collections care procedures for the Southern Appalachian collection of documents, photographs, oral history audiotapes, music recordings, and other materials held by the Ramsey Center for Regional Studies of Mars Hill College.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Housing of James H. and Candace A. Van Alen Collection
ProjectDesc: The National Endowment for the Humanities Preservation Assistance Grant would support the purchase of preservation supplies needed to properly house the James H. and Candace A.Van Alen Collection. It is a rather large collection encompassing 105 cubic feet of material; a good portion of that being photographic materials. We have done what we can to stabilize the collection through sorting, reboxing, and isolating items with mold and fire damage. We are now focusing on the proper housing for long term storage. The NEH Preservation Assistance Grant would help us to properly house the Van Alen Collection in preservation quality photo sleeves, tissue, file folders, boxes, etc.
ToSupport: The purchase of preservation supplies to rehouse the James H. and Candace A. Van Alen Collection, composed mostly of still images, that document the history and culture of Newport, Rhode Island, since the 1850s.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment and Environmental Monitoring of Archival Collections
ProjectDesc: Louisville, KY's Portland Museum is seeking support to engage Gregory Farmer to conduct an updated preservation assessment, review collections work accomplished by volunteers, and provide guidance to Board and staff. The updated preservation assesment will set priorities and draft a long-range plan for the care of the Museum's collections. In addition, the Musem is seeking support for supplies and small equipment. The Museum's collections represent the history of an inner-city neigborhood that was once an independent rivertown at the Falls of the Ohio River. It is a community of need.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment and the purchase of environmental monitoring equipment, storage enclosures, and disaster recovery supplies for artifacts, art, oral histories, and print collections that document the history of a riverside inner-city neighborhood in Louisville, Kentucky, from the 1820s to the present.

ProjectTitle: Storage Upgrade Project
ProjectDesc: As part of Mission San Juan Capistrano's Five-Year Strategic Plan, the museum facilities will be upgraded and the collections preserved. To this end, the Mission recently participated in the Conservation Assessment Program (CAP), hiring the conservator John Griswold to carry out a general conservation assessment. One of the high-priority recommendations made by Mr. Griswold in his final report included upgrading storage facilities. If awarded, this grant will cover an initial, yet very important phase of improving collections storage by providing cabinetry and shelving, preservation supplies, environmental monitoring equipment, and training.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage supplies, furniture, and environmental monitoring equipment and the training of staff to improve the care of the museum's 2000 artifacts, which date from the 18th through the 20th century and document Native American, Mission, and Rancho life in southern California.

ProjectTitle: Development of a Collections Storage Plan
ProjectDesc: SSRHS will prepare a collections storage plan, the most critical priority identified in the recently-completed CAP Survey. Information will be collected through a) on-site assessments (at SSRHS and prospective off-site storage facilities); b) meetings with staff, key board members and volunteers; and c) review of relevant documents. The collected information will be used to identify: appropriate storage procedures and furniture/equipment to house the collections, and a suitable facility to store a portion of the collection off-site. This project will improve care of the collections and make them more accessible for use in exhibits, education, publications and research.
ToSupport: Consultation with a preservation professional to develop a plan for improving the storage of collections documenting the history of a Chesapeake Bay community.

ProjectTitle: Preservation of the Collection housed in the Historic Norlin Library
ProjectDesc: University of Colorado at Boulder Libraries is seeking support to enhance the preservation of the collections housed in the historic Norlin Library. Norlin Library houses the core collections in humanities and social sciences, the Special Collections, Archives, and Government documents. A recent environmental monitoring program has revealed humidity problems in areas where some of the most valuable parts of the collection are house. We are seeking funding to have Garrison/Lull, Inc. a nationally recognized expert in building environments review our findings, inspect the air handlers involved, and make specific recommendations to improve the HVAC system.
ToSupport: A consultation with an expert who will diagnose problems with humidity instability in the university's Norlin Library and recommend options to improve the air handling system.

ProjectTitle: Assessing Environmental Conditions at Smith's Castle
ProjectDesc: The Cocumscussoc Association at Smith’s Castle requests funding from the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH), to support a consultation concerning the problems of a severely damp basement in The Castle’s 17th century foundation. The moisture and accompanying humidity affects the building’s walls and the collections within; mold on the collections, walls and moldings is a visible example of the problem.
ToSupport: Consultation to assess environmental conditions that contribute to high relative humidity and mold in Smith's Castle, a National Register garrison-style trading post dating from 1678 that houses collections of 18th- and 19th-century furniture and paintings, bed coverings, clothing and accessories, decorative arts, and works of art on paper.
Participants: Kari Van Buren [Project Director]; Neil Dunay [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment of Archival Materials
ProjectDesc: This Assistance Grant will help the Society establish a formal system for the preservation of the items in our care, bringing us closer to fulfilling several long-range goals. In 2004, a collections policy was adopted by the board of directors. In January '05, we purchased the Past Perfect software and began cataloging our collections. Hiring a preservation specialist to assess the collection and devise a plan for its storage and care is the next step. The Museum Society’s collections are a priority for 2005. The assistance grant will keep us moving forward, creating greater access to the collection for researchers and the public.
ToSupport: A general preservation assessment of corporate records, photographs, books, and ephemera related to the cigar-making industry in Tampa, Florida.

ProjectTitle: Collections Management Workshop and Purchase of Archival Supplies
ProjectDesc: The Oregon Nikkei Legacy Center will hold a one day collections management workshop for volunteers and staff. The workshop will provide training in proper care and storage methods for many types of artifacts and review collections cataloging and record keeping methods. Archival supplies and materials will be purchased to provide for the upgrade of storage for the collections. ONLC maintains a collection of national interest that documents the history of Issei immigration and contributions to the settlement, economy, and civic life of Oregon and the surrounding region. The collections room and shelving is new and very suitable, and this grant will provide the hands on training and archival supplies so urgently needed.
ToSupport: A preservation workshop for the center's staff and volunteers to improve the care of collections that document Issei immigration, the events during World War II related to the evacuation of Japanese Americans from the West Coast, and their return to Oregon after the war.

ProjectTitle: Rehousing Coverlet Collection
ProjectDesc: The Yager Museum is requesting funds to purchase two rolled textile storage racks form the Borroughs Corporation. The racks will be used to store the museum's collection of twenty-two 19th century coverlets. The new storage units will allow the museum to properly care for the hand-made coverlets, which are important historical works from the surrounding region. Currently, 14 coverlets are rolled and mounted on a wall using L-brackets, the remainder are stored folded and stacked on open metal shelving.
ToSupport: Purchasing storage furniture to rehouse the Yager Museum's 19th-century textiles that depict art and daily life in the mid-Atlantic region.

ProjectTitle: Baton Rouge Room Archival Management Assessment
ProjectDesc: The East Baton Rouge Parish Library is in the earliest phase of discussion regarding the design and construction of a new Main Library, which will house the Baton Rouge Room's local archival history collection. A general preservation assessment of the collection's current condition and future needs is crucial. The Library proposes to hire a qualified archivist to assess our present storage and environmental conditions, space requirements, preservation materials used, security, and public access policies. The archivist's findings and recommendations will serve to guide the plans for a new facility, in accordance with the collection's current and future needs.
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of archives, manuscripts, photographs, maps, and oral history collections related to the history of Baton Rouge and the surrounding area from the 18th through the 20th century.

ProjectTitle: Preservation Assessment to Preserve the Library's Engelberg Collection
ProjectDesc: Conception Abbey & Seminary Library is seeking a Preservation Assistance Grant to engage a consultant for a General Preservation Assessment for its Engelberg Collection. We have a culturally significant collection of 2000 volumes from monastery of Engelberg in Switzerland largely printed in the 15th-18th centuries including fifty incunables. This collection is currently housed on wooden shelves in conditions that are not optimal for the long-term preservation of the books. The consultant would visit our library to assess its policies, practices, and the conditions affecting the care and preservation of our collection, and prepare a report that would summarize findings and contain prioritized recommendations for future preservation action
ToSupport: A preservation assessment of the policies, practices, and conditions affecting the Engelberg Collection, a collection of 2000 theological works dating from the 15th to the 18th century, which was developed by a Swiss abbey (established 1120) and acquired by the seminary in the 1870s.

ProjectTitle: Purchase of Storage Furniture and Supplies
ProjectDesc: The Historic Hillsborough Commission’s (HHC)collection, located at the Burwell School Historic Site in a 19th c. structure that served as an antebellum girls’ school, constitutes a comprehensive collection of information on the Burwell Family, enslaved people, the Burwell School, its students, the town of Hillsborough, and the HHC. These documents are crucial to scholars, townspeople and the HHC for research, interpretation and programming that serve the community at-large. HHC is applying for a $4068 grant for the purchase of metal storage cabinets, an archival quality map case, archival document boxes, and other archival supplies. These purchases are fundamental to the preservation, accessibility and continued growth of HHC’s archives.
ToSupport: The purchase of storage furniture and preservation supplies to rehouse manuscripts, maps, books, photographs, and artifacts related to the founding and operation of Burwell Female School, 1837 to 1857.

ProjectTitle: Textile Conservation Assessment

These textiles will be surveyed on an object by object basis to identify treatment priorities and make suggestions for rehousing. A group survey of an additional 500 lower priority items will identify storage and conservation needs. The assessment will be completed by textile conservator Julia Brennan in conjunction with Ann Steuart, Associate Curator at Tudor Place.
ToSupport: Hiring a consultant to conduct a conservation assessment of 1,200 textiles, which include articles of clothing and household furnishings and linens associated with Martha Washington and her descendants, to develop a conservation treatment plan, and to assess storage needs of the collection.

CCAHA will provide guidance, assessment tools, and technical information to assist in the completion of the specially tailored emergency preparedness and response plan.
ToSupport: The development of an emergency preparedness and response plan to safeguard print and artifact collections that document the history of Germans in Pennsylvania.

The grant will launch this project by funding the purchase of materials necessary for the conservation of the Special Collections Department’s images related to the history of Trinity University and its relationship with three historic Texas cities (Tehuacana, Waxahachie, and San Antonio). This project follows a conservationist's formal survey in 2003 and the drafting of the Coating Library's disaster plan.
ToSupport: The purchase of preservation supplies to rehouse glass plate, tintype, and gelatin images, slides, and other photographs related to the university's history and to life in San Antonio and in other south Texas cities and towns from 1869 to the present.

ProjectTitle: The Study Center at the Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art, Cornell University
ProjectDesc: The Herbert F. Johnson Museum of Art at Cornell University is planning to build an extension--the Study Center--on the north side of the current museum building, a landmark structure designed by I.M. Pei in 1973; the architect-in-charge for that building was John Sullivan, who still works for Mr. Pei's firm, Pei Cobb Freed. The Study Center is being designed by Mr. Sullivan, working closely with I.M. Pei. The Study Center will have, on two levels, a total of 13,000 gross square feet, or about 9,000 net square feet. The Study Center will include several important functions, all of which will enhance the impact of the humanities on this campus and which are central to our current five-year plan: a public gallery, for special exhibitions and for selections from the permanent collection; open, or "visible" storage, for the display of large numbers of works from the collection with computer work stations and reference materials; a lecture room, seminar room, workshop room, and library; closed storage, for the Asian collection and other parts of the collections; and curatorial and education offices. Programming in the Study Center will include courses for university students, for schoolchildren, and for adults; free gallery handouts and other materials; a Palm Pilot tour of open storage; and demonstrations and workshops, among other activities. These programs will be supervised by a half-time endowed program coordinator for the Study Center. In this way, the Johnson Museum will become the laboratory for the humanities on this campus. We are applying to the National Endowment for the Humanities for $500,000, to be matched by $2,000,000, for a total of $2,500,000. Of this amount, $1,000,000 would be used for construction costs, and $1,500,000 would be used as endowment for programming.
ToSupport: Construction of a study center in the university's art museum and endowment for educational programming and salary for a half-time education coordinator.
Disciplines: Art History and Criticism; Museum Studies or Historical Preservation

These collections, consisting of a library, archives, artifact reference specimens, slides, prints and drawings, represent an invaluable resource for the study of the history, archaeology, art history, religion, and related humanistic disciplines concerning Cyprus and adjacent eastern Mediterranean regions. CAARI's research facilities are used annually by a broad and varied community of local and international scholars and students. The added space will provide both reading and storage space, which is projected to meet the needs of the institute far into the foreseeable future. CAARI is seeking an NEH Challenge Grant totaling $2 million to support the construction of the addition and to create an endowment that will provide income that will be used toward the increased costs of operating an enlarged facility.

Institution: Fredericksburg Area Museum and Cultural Center, Inc.
ProjectTitle: NEH Challenge Grant for Endowment for the Fredericksburg Area Museum and Cultural Center
ProjectDesc: The Fredericksburg Area Museum and Cultural Center (FAMCC) collects and interprets the history and culture of a significant community in the mid-Atlantic region, and the museum offers the only comprehensive story of the region's past. No longer just an outer commuter suburb of the nation's capital, Fredericksburg today is at the forefront of the nation's next big demographic movement. As a rapidly growing "exurb," the region we interpret has the power to tell a broad American story, linking a varied past with the current major transformation in the way Americans organize their society. The museum itself has matured since opening in 1988, but it, too, like its community is poised for further change. Our strategic plan sets a goal to enlarge the museum's collection, number of exhibitions, and offering of public programs, and to expand the humanities base of interpretation by presenting the history of the region within a larger intellectual framework. As we engage in a self-study for re-accreditation, and bring to bear the results of a $7.5 million campaign, we have reached the critical mass of resources and conceptual willingness to transform how we interpret the history of Fredericksburg. The capital campaign jump started the process and has funded key changes to strengthen the humanities by adding humanities staff and humanities scholars. The FAMCC seeks an NEH Challenge Grant of $400,000 to leverage an additional $1,200,000 for an endowment to sustain these changes. Specifically, endowment income from the Challenge Grant and its match will enable the museum to (a) endow two humanities positions--a full-time school programs coordinator (now half-time) and a new half-time public programs coordinator, (b) redesign the museum's website to incorporate new components on the history of the region for the public and for school programs, and (c) have sustained use of humanities scholars after campaign funds expire.
ToSupport: Endowment for staff coordinators for school and public programs, as well as website development and stipends for humanities scholars.
Participants: Edwin Watson [Project Director]; Ellen Killough [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Levine Museum of the New South Endowment Campaign
ProjectDesc: Levine Museum of the New South requests a $500,000 NEH Challenge Grant to be matched by $1.5 million in new private gifts to establish a $2 million endowment that will 1) support ground-breaking research on post-Civil War Southern history and culture that leads to exhibitions and public programs and 2) expand community outreach through humanities programming and institute new professionally developed evaluation of all exhibits and programs to measure the impact and effectiveness of learning through Museum activities. The Museum has grown steadily since its founding in 1991, and has established a distinguished record of exhibitions and activities that use history to promote civic dialogue and help Americans understand how the past influences the present and can guide decisions about the future. The endowment will ensure permanent, consistent funding for these activities, and launch the Museum toward more ambitious projects that would not be possible without additional support.
ToSupport: Endowment for research on post-Civil War Southern history and expanded community outreach through humanities programming.

The Council is conducting an $800,000 capital campaign to pay for the facility, renovate it for VHC programs and provide $100,000 of new endowment. This $200,000 NEH challenge grant application is an essential part of that campaign. Reduced operating costs and income from the new endowment will provide funds for new and expanded program initiatives as well.
ToSupport: Purchase and renovation of a new facility for the Vermont Humanities Council, and endowment for programs.

ProjectTitle: Remote Sensing and GIS Training and Research for Iraqi Archaeologists
ProjectDesc: This project focuses on a four-month training program in Remote Sensing and GIS for professional Iraqi archaeologists drawn from the State Board of Antiquities and Baghdad and Mosul Universities. The course will focus on the utility of these techniques for research, site protection and site management. By the end of the program, the faculty will have the skills to teach these materials on their return to Iraq. Coincident with the training program, we will survey archaeological sites in the key Nippur, Uruk and Eridu survey areas using recent high resolution Digital Globe imagery for evidence of site damage from looting and development, recording new sites, ancient landscape features and intra-site details.
ToSupport: An intensive training program for two faculty members each from Baghdad and Mosul Universities and two members of the Iraqi State Board of Antiquities and Heritage in remote sensing and geographic information systems (GIS).

ProjectTitle: National History Competition
ProjectDesc: The purpose of the project is to create and evaluate a two-year pilot program for a National American History Competition for middle-school students, grades 6-8. The pilot program has the potential to grow into a multi-million dollar national competition down the road. Dr. Peter Gibbon, the principal investigator, will lead a consortium comprising the Boston University School of Education, the National Council for History Education, the Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History, and the National History Club to accomplish the goals of this pilot program. The principal consultants for this project would be Dr Bill Ross of the National Council for History Education in Westlake, Ohio, and Dr. John Patrick, Professor Emeritus at Indiana University, Bloomington. Meetings of the three will occur in Westlake, Ohio and Bloomington, Indiana.
ToSupport: Two-year pilot testing of a National History Competition for elementary and middle-school students to determine whether such a competition has the potential to be offered on a national scale.

ProjectTitle: Archaeological Field Data from UC Berkeley Expedition to Nineveh: 1987, 1989, 1990
ToSupport: The creation of a digital database of field documentation from the university's archaeological survey and selected excavations at the ancient Mesopotamian city of Nineveh (7th millennium into 1st millennium BCE) that were conducted in 1987, 1989, and 1990.
Participants: David Stronach [Project Director]; Eleanor Wilkinson [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: The Iraqi Jewish Archive
ProjectDesc: The Center for Jewish History is seeking funding for a project to ensure the preservation and accessibility of the recently discovered Iraqi Jewish Archive. With more than 500,000 volumes and 100 million documents and artifacts on its campus and access to myriad catalog entries related to archives of the Jewish community, the Center for Jewish History is well poised to oversee the following activities: Creation of an inventory database to document the Archive’s contents; Photograph digitally title pages so that the items can be catalogued; Assure a basic item level conservation assessment by experts in the field; and preserve a small number of items in the archive to demonstrate the feasibility of conserving the entire archive.
ToSupport: The creation of an item-level collection assessment and inventory database of books and documents in Hebrew, Judeo-Arabic, and Arabic that provide evidence of the history and culture of the Jewish community in Iraq since 762 BCE. A sample of the variety of paper-based materials in the archives would be conserved as a testbed for a future phase of the project.
Participants: Robert Sink [Project Director]; Laura Leone [Project Director]

ProjectTitle: Training Preservation Administrators and Conservators to Preserve the Nation's Humanities Collections
ProjectDesc: This project will continue and enhance the Preservation and Conservation Studies (PCS) program at the School of Information, The Univ. of Texas at Austin. PCS is the only source of comprehensive education & training for preservation administrators & conservators for library & archival collections. PCS's strength is producing knowledgeable, educated, persuasive professionals to lead at the institutional, consortial, & funding agency levels to chart the course of library & archives preservation for the 21st century. The program uniquely focuses on the needs of whole collections significant for education & scholarly research in the humanities. Graduates receive a Master's degree in information science with an Endorsement of Specialization in Preservation Administration or a Certificate
ToSupport: The education of preservation administrators and conservators in the care of library and archival collections in the humanities.

Institution: SUNY Research Foundation, Buffalo State College
ProjectTitle: Graduate Training Program for Conservators
